artigo.texto: Rondo Energy and Rio Tinto Advance Australia's Largest Thermal Energy Storage Project GLADSTONE, Australia, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rondo Energy and Rio Tinto have started front-end engineering and design on the project for a 360 MWh storage / 30 MW discharge Rondo Heat Battery, supported by a grant from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA). ARENA's funding for the project will be provided in stages, with an initial $3.6 million to complete front-end engineering and design work. Following successful completion of that study, ARENA will provide up to $38 million for deployment. ARENA has also approved up to $33.3 million in conditional contingency support, which would only be made available in defined circumstances to manage specific project risks, including cost overruns and electricity costs. If progressed, the project would be delivered at Rio Tinto's Yarwun alumina refinery near Gladstone, Queensland and would be one of the first large-scale demonstrations of thermal energy storage for industrial process heat globally, and a world-first for the alumina industry. Rondo Heat Batteries use abundant, low-cost midday electricity to charge, storing energy as high-temperature heat in refractory brick, and supplying energy as 24/7 continuous process heat to industry. Typically, the heat is delivered as steam, directly into an industrial facility's steam network. Australia regularly has 4-6 hours of surplus solar-generated renewable electricity in the middle of the day, but industrial facilities need heat 24 hours a day, not just when the sun is shining. By charging when electricity is cheap and abundant and discharging continuously, Rondo Heat Batteries turn short periods of low-cost electricity into 24/7 delivery of low-cost steam. For energy-intensive industries such as alumina refining, Rondo Heat Batteries create a pathway to electrification that addresses both emissions and energy costs. Because the heat battery slots into the existing steam network, the facility's processes run exactly as before — the only thing that changes is the energy for that heat: no longer from fossil fuels, but sourced from low cost electricity instead. The Yarwun study will assess the technical and economic viability of integrating the technology into refinery operations. "This project shows how Australia's abundant energy can become a competitive advantage for industry," said Dr. Kira Rundel, Rondo's Head of Australia. "Heat batteries allow manufacturers to use low-cost electricity to produce the reliable, round-the-clock heat their operations need. Australia's largest heat battery will show how factories can cut emissions without increasing energy costs, helping Australian industry to increase global competitiveness and supporting local manufacturing jobs." Rio Tinto Pacific Operations Managing Director Armando Torres said: "Reducing emissions from alumina refining is complex, particularly when it comes to generating the high-pressure steam needed for our operations. "This study will help us determine whether thermal energy storage can provide a technically and economically viable alternative to fossil fuels for part of Yarwun's steam requirements. "The best way to tackle challenges of this scale is through collaboration between industry, government, and technology partners. We welcome ARENA and Rondo's support as we assess technologies that could help reduce our Scope 1 emissions while maintaining reliable operations at Yarwun." About Rondo Energy Rondo Energy delivers firm heat and power, including combined heat and power (CHP), to heavy industry and provides power solutions and long duration storage to data centers. For industrial heat applications, Rondo Heat Batteries convert 4-6 hours of low-cost electricity into continuous 24-hour, high-temperature heat, delivered as steam or hot air up to 1,000°C. The heat delivered integrates directly with existing industrial equipment and processes, eliminating on-site emissions and running on lower cost energy. Rondo heat storage can integrate with steam turbines to deliver combined heat and power (CHP) for industry, and long duration power-to-power solutions for large energy consumers such as data centers. Built on proven refractory brick as the thermal storage medium, Rondo's platform is engineered for multi-decade operation in the most demanding industrial environments. Rondo Heat Batteries have been delivering firm heat and power at scale since 2023, with operational facilities serving customers in fuels and cement (including steam driving turbines for electricity) in the United States and in Asia. The next unit will come online shortly - a 100 MWh Rondo Heat Battery under construction in Europe for a chemical plant. Rondo is a global company based in California, with teams across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia. Providing heat and power solutions to the alumina industry is an area of focus for the company due to the strong fit of Rondo's technology with the heat and power needs of the alumina industry. artigo.texto: As concessionárias de transmissão de energia elétrica podem participar dos leilões de reserva de capacidade com sistemas de armazenamento em baterias (BESS), desde que obtenham autorização prévia da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) e cumpram condições previstas nos contratos de concessão. Entre elas está a demonstração de benefícios para os consumidores, com a possibilidade de reversão total ou parcial das receitas obtidas com a nova atividade para a modicidade tarifária. O entendimento é da Procuradoria Federal junto à Aneel, que analisou a possibilidade de atuação das transmissoras no segmento de armazenamento a partir de uma consulta envolvendo a Taesa. A companhia solicitou à agência a ratificação de seu entendimento de que poderia disputar futuros leilões de reserva de capacidade na forma de potência (LRCap) com sistemas de armazenamento autônomos. A Procuradoria concluiu que não há proibição legal para que transmissoras desenvolvam atividades fora do objeto de suas concessões, diferentemente das restrições expressas impostas às distribuidoras. A participação nos certames, contudo, não é automática e depende das condições estabelecidas nos contratos de transmissão. A Taesa discorda de parte desse entendimento. Em posicionamento enviado à MegaWhat, a companhia afirmou que o marco regulatório já dispõe de mecanismos suficientes para permitir a participação dos agentes, sem a necessidade de uma exigência adicional de autorização contratual prévia. A transmissora também contesta a classificação das receitas fixas dos contratos de armazenamento como receitas acessórias da transmissão. Segundo a empresa, os empreendimentos possuem patrimônio, contabilidade, financiamento, obrigações e outorgas próprios, o que justificaria o tratamento independente dessas receitas. Em agosto, a Aneel autorizou a ISA Energia Brasil a explorar atividades atípicas relacionadas à prestação de serviços de eficiência energética e uso racional da energia para clientes B2B, utilizando sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias (BESS). O aval contemplo uma atividade econômica diferente daquelas diretamente previstas nos contratos de concessão de transmissão da empresa. Como não havia regulamentação específica da agência sobre a prestação desse tipo de serviço, foi necessário solicitar anuência. Transmissoras poderão atuar por meio de subsidiárias O parecer considera juridicamente admissível que concessionárias de transmissão participem dos leilões de baterias por meio de subsidiárias ou sociedades de propósito específico (SPEs) com objeto social próprio. Essa estrutura, no entanto, não dispensa a autorização regulatória. Segundo a Procuradoria, o exercício de atividades fora do objeto da concessão depende de anuência prévia da Aneel, independentemente de ocorrer diretamente pela transmissora ou por meio de outra empresa controlada. A análise tomou como referência cláusulas do contrato de concessão nº 05/2023 da Taesa, que permitem o desenvolvimento de outras atividades empresariais, desde que observadas as exigências regulatórias. Entre as condições apontadas estão a manutenção de registros contábeis, demonstrações financeiras, fluxos de caixa, contratos e relatórios gerenciais individualizados, de forma a impedir a confusão patrimonial entre a concessão de transmissão e os negócios de armazenamento. A fiscalização dessas condições caberia à Superintendência de Fiscalização Econômica e Financeira (SFF) da Aneel. O parecer também destaca que, em regra, a responsabilidade da transmissora como sócia ou controladora de uma SPE de armazenamento ficaria limitada à sua participação e à integralização do capital social da subsidiária. Receitas de baterias podem ser revertidas O parecer também descreve a necessidade de que a participação das transmissoras em atividades de armazenamento poderá produzir benefícios econômicos para a concessão e, consequentemente, para os usuários do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). A Procuradoria aponta que a autorização deverá estar condicionada à preservação da modicidade tarifária, mediante reversão total ou parcial das receitas obtidas com a nova atividade, conforme as disposições do contrato de concessão analisado. Para o órgão, o pedido poderá ser deferido caso fique demonstrado, de maneira objetiva e juridicamente vinculante, que a exploração do armazenamento por meio de uma subsidiária produzirá benefícios econômicos concretos para a concessão. A avaliação caberá à Aneel, que deve considerar as circunstâncias específicas de cada pedido e o interesse público, especialmente a continuidade da prestação do serviço de transmissão e a modicidade tarifária. Taesa contesta exigências para participar dos leilões A Taesa afirmou à MegaWhat que vem desenvolvendo estudos para avaliar oportunidades de negócios relacionadas aos sistemas de armazenamento de energia. A companhia considera que a tecnologia é necessária para o avanço da transição energética e para aumentar a resiliência e a confiabilidade das redes de transmissão e distribuição. Segundo a empresa, o mercado brasileiro de armazenamento ainda está em desenvolvimento e parte das regras permanece em construção. Nesse contexto, a transmissora entende que o posicionamento sobre a necessidade de anuência prévia e sobre a classificação dos contratos de armazenamento como receitas acessórias ocorreu em caráter preliminar e precisa ser aprofundado à luz do arcabouço regulatório aplicável. Na avaliação da Taesa, os mecanismos de controle e as salvaguardas já existentes são suficientes para assegurar a participação dos agentes, sem a imposição de um requisito adicional de autorização contratual prévia. A companhia também sustenta que as receitas fixas provenientes dos contratos dos leilões de reserva de capacidade são juridicamente independentes das receitas da transmissão. artigo.texto: Gelion shares jump 21% after US laboratory validates battery technology Published: 05:30 19 Oct 2026 EDT Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF, FRA:X0S) shares jumped 21% to 16p on Monday after independent testing by the National Laboratory of the Rockies validated key performance characteristics of its next-generation battery technology. The battery materials developer reported preliminary results showing that its Nano-Encapsulated Sulfur (NES) cells retained 92% of their reference capacity despite a 20-fold increase in cycling rate. The findings strengthen the technical evidence behind Gelion’s efforts to commercialise its sulfur-based cathode material for applications requiring high energy capacity and rapid power delivery. The laboratory independently fabricated electrodes using Gelion’s material, assembled coin cells and reproduced key electrochemical results previously observed in the company’s own facilities. The tests confirmed comparable voltage profiles, sulfur utilisation and capacity retention during cycling, demonstrating that the material’s performance could be replicated outside Gelion’s laboratories. The results also complement earlier testing by QinetiQ, which demonstrated sustained high-power operation in independently assembled battery cells under conditions representative of drone cruising and vertical take-off and landing. Gelion is working with the American laboratory under a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement announced in June, which aims to advance its technology towards commercial qualification. The next stage includes developing and testing larger pouch-cell prototypes, moving beyond initial material-level validation toward batteries suitable for practical applications. The programme also aims to support eventual qualification for American government and defence procurement, alongside the development of domestic battery manufacturing capabilities. The latest results follow two automotive developments in October, when Gelion announced a co-funded evaluation programme with a top-five global carmaker on 13 October and a separate material transfer agreement with a top-15 manufacturer on 6 October. The company has also secured a development and scale-up agreement with the Japanese advanced materials group Mitsui Kinzoku, which includes £2 million in staged payments to advance its sulfur battery technology.

artigo.texto: BYD's 515 kW Tang EV Filing Lands Alongside a 22% Share Decline and Shrinking Export Buffer Published on 10/19/2026 at 06:01 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD is pressing ahead with a twin-track strategy of rapid model renewal at home and deeper manufacturing roots abroad, even as its shares trade deep in negative territory for the year. The stock closed Friday at EUR 8.34, down 22% since the start of January. Regulatory filings published Friday by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) offered the first official performance figures for a new all-wheel-drive generation of the Tang EV. The five-seat SUV will carry two electric motors — a 215 kW unit up front and a 300 kW rear axle — for a combined peak output of 515 kW. Top speed is listed at 250 km/h. The documents did not disclose battery capacity, range or charging specifications for the all-wheel-drive variant. Da Han EV Joins the Line-Up With Second-Generation Blade Cells The Tang filing follows the formal market launch of the Da Han EV, which arrives in three battery-electric trim levels priced between 235,900 and 275,900 yuan. Every version uses a 102.3 kWh second-generation Blade battery that BYD says delivers up to 1,008 kilometres of range on China's CLTC test cycle, with a 10-to-97% charge achievable in nine minutes. A LiDAR-based driver-assistance system is fitted as well. The product cadence shows no sign of slowing. On Friday, BYD manager Lu Tian shared images of the third-generation Qin PLUS after the model cleared regulatory registration in China, with media reports pointing to a market launch expected in late October. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Nine-Month Deliveries Slip 3.94% Those technical upgrades are meeting a tougher commercial backdrop. BYD delivered 3,131,576 new-energy vehicles over the first nine months of the year, a 3.94% decline from the same period a year earlier. September alone accounted for 463,561 NEVs, including 456,713 passenger cars, with exports contributing 180,700 units. Britain stood out as a bright spot: 20,140 new registrations in September made it BYD's strongest month and strongest quarter in that market to date, according to the company. Trade Barriers Bite Into Export Economics Policy shifts are clouding the export outlook. A deal between the European Union and China caps imported hybrid vehicles at 350,000 units a year. Roughly a week ago, China's finance ministry also announced it will cut the value-added tax rebate on exports of alternative-drive vehicles from 13% to 9% effective April 1, 2027 — a change that could squeeze exporter margins. Rising tariffs and trade hurdles are pushing Chinese manufacturers to build production capacity directly in their target markets. UOB Kay Hian flagged on October 9 that these barriers are intensifying the pressure toward localised manufacturing. Media reports indicate BYD plans to grow its European headcount to around 40,000 employees by 2030, strengthening sales and production operations across the continent. Analyst Backs the Stock Despite a Soft Home Market The same brokerage cut its sales forecasts for Chinese automakers for 2026 through 2028, citing weakness at home, where expiring tax incentives and higher fuel prices are weighing particularly on the combustion-engine segment. Even so, UOB Kay Hian reiterated a buy rating on BYD on October 9 and kept the stock as its sector favourite, despite the Chinese auto industry's weaker-than-expected nine-month figures. Whether the latest generation of technical upgrades can offset margin pressure on exports is the question that will shape the coming quarters. artigo.texto: BYD Ties Its European Future to 3,000 Fast Chargers as Deliveries Ease Published on 10/20/2026 at 06:41 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD is betting that the infrastructure behind the electric car matters as much as the vehicle itself. At the Paris Motor Show, the Chinese group laid out plans to install 3,000 fast-charging stations across Europe by the end of 2027, a build-out meant to win buyers over to its own rapid-charging technology. The announcement came alongside new metal: the seven-seat ATTO 8 flagship SUV and the second generation of the company's Blade battery, shown together with models from its Denza brand. The ATTO 8 will be the first BYD model in Europe to carry the flash-charging system. Its second-generation Blade pack, rated at 115 kilowatt-hours, is designed for a range of up to 653 kilometers on the WLTP cycle. European launch is slated for the first quarter of 2027. A Wider Push Beyond Passenger Cars The charging pledge is only one strand of a broader international strategy. BYD Energy Storage, the group's battery-storage arm, unveiled a global after-sales network for its storage systems. The structure spans nine operations and maintenance centers and draws on more than 200 field engineers, with additional sites in South Africa and Bulgaria already scheduled for 2027. Over 100 research and development specialists are tied into the network, a move aimed at giving commercial customers technical support well after installation and reinforcing confidence in the reliability of BYD's storage products. Headcount in Europe is climbing in step with the expansion. Stella Li, the group's executive vice chair, told Bloomberg that the European workforce will soon pass 10,000 employees, with roughly 40,000 planned for the region by 2030. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? New Models for China and a Safety Nod At home, BYD introduced the Da Han, an electric flagship sedan built on a 1,000-volt architecture that delivers up to 1,008 kilometers of range on the CLTC cycle. The entry version is priced at 235,900 yuan. The Seagull, meanwhile, entered its second generation on the Chinese market on Tuesday, growing in size and gaining lidar-based driver assistance, according to media reports. On the safety front, the SHARK DMO pickup secured a five-star rating in Euro NCAP crash tests. Software is another front. A strategic partnership with smartphone maker Honor will link the YOYO voice and AI assistant directly to BYD's DiLink system through an agent-to-agent protocol. Media reports suggest the integration is intended for more than 100 of the group's models — a reminder that seamless connection to users' digital lives has become a core selling point in China's fiercely competitive market. Mixed Deliveries, Muted Shares Sales momentum has been uneven. BYD shipped 3,131,576 new-energy vehicles between January and September, down 3.94% from the same period a year earlier. September alone accounted for 463,561 units, of which 180,700 went to export markets. Investors have taken the operational news in stride. The stock slipped 0.1% to EUR 8.33 in today's trading, extending its decline since the turn of the year to 22%. Monday's close of EUR 8.30, a 0.5% daily loss, left the shares just about 3.3% above their 52-week low. A clearer picture may emerge on October 29, 2026, when the board meets to review and approve the unaudited third-quarter figures. artigo.texto: BYD's Overseas Battery Surge Meets a 350,000-Vehicle Ceiling in Europe Published on 10/21/2026 at 05:11 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD's expansion story is running on two tracks that don't move in step. New figures show its battery installations outside China climbing sharply, while at home the volume and market share both slipped. On the vehicle side, a fresh trade understanding between Brussels and Beijing has put a number on how many hybrids can flow into Europe each year. A tale of two battery markets Data from SNE Research cited in an October 15 report put BYD's overseas battery installations at 39.7 GWh for the period covered — a 66.5% jump on the same stretch a year earlier. That growth stands in contrast to a softer home market, though it says nothing about how many cars BYD is shipping abroad. The distinction matters: a strong battery business does not by itself answer questions about vehicle demand. Inside China, installations reached 106.44 GWh, down 4.3% year on year, with a market share of 18.53%. The domestic share fell 4.04 percentage points. So both the installed volume and the relative position weakened at home, even as the overseas picture brightened — the regional split within the battery unit is widening. Europe sets a hard limit The vehicle business faces a different set of constraints. On October 13, BYD shares came under pressure as investors weighed export prospects and margins after the European Union and China agreed to cap Chinese hybrid imports. Reuters reported an annual ceiling of 350,000 vehicles. On top of that, Beijing plans to cut the export tax rebate for alternative-drive vehicles from 13% to 9%. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? The two measures bite in different places. The import cap limits access to the European market by volume; the lower rebate sits behind the margin concerns that were reported. Neither figure, on its own, allows a specific earnings impact for BYD to be calculated. Malaysia: a partner named, a start date missing In Southeast Asia, BYD is pushing local assembly and distribution forward on several fronts. BYD Malaysia named Inokom in Kulim as its assembly partner on Thursday, a deal covering local assembly from shipped vehicle kits — an extension of BYD's Malaysian activities beyond sales, though not evidence that production has begun. No model has been fixed and no start date confirmed, so the economic contribution remains an open question. Distribution is further along. A new outlet opened yesterday in Rawang, Selangor, operated by BE Autohaus — another BYD site for the BE Group after Setia Alam and Kota Kemuning. BYD Sime Motors runs 45 sales and marketing outlets nationwide, 33 service facilities and 16 body-and-paint centres, so the new location slots into a network covering both vehicle sales and after-sales care. An opening promotion in Rawang runs from 19 to 30 October 2026, with test drives and offers on selected models. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Philippines: tariff relief, currency drag On the Philippines, BYD is backing an extension of duty-free EV imports through 2040; under the existing rule the exemption ends in 2028. The terms for imported vehicles therefore remain a key variable for regional expansion. AB Capital Securities also flags a weak peso as a possible risk to import costs and margins — growing sales and a broader dealer network don't erase such pressures on their own. Ayala/BYD sales reached 28,399 vehicles through August 2026, already ahead of the full-year 2025 total. The pieces of BYD's Southeast Asian build-out are tangible but unevenly advanced. In the Philippines, sales sit alongside an unresolved tariff question. In Malaysia, the retail network is growing while local assembly waits on specifics about model and production timing. What counts for investors is not the tally of new locations but whether they turn into durable business. Ad BYD Stock: New Analysis - 21 October Fresh BYD information released. artigo.texto: BEIJING, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — CATL today unveiled the innovative dual-electric range extension battery and the latest generation of heavy-duty battery-swapping solution to accelerate the electrification of road freight transportation. Competition in electric heavy-duty trucking is moving beyond technical specifications toward full-lifecycle value. While battery swapping has made energy replenishment faster and more predictable, concerns about battery utilization, operating costs and residual vehicle value continue to affect fleet economics. To address these challenges, CATL combines its dual-electric range extension battery with QIJI’s strategy of standardization, new infrastructure and a full commercial ecosystem, bringing battery swapping and industry-wide collaboration together to accelerate heavy-duty truck electrification. A Dual-Electric Approach to Range Extension CATL’s dual-electric range extension battery combines two independent yet complementary battery systems. The main battery uses QIJI’s standardized chassis-mounted swappable battery to maximize efficiency. A behind-the-cab range-extension power system, currently equipped with a 77kWh battery capable of 3C charging, provides backup power. Together, the systems maintain uninterrupted power delivery and provide redundancy for demanding operating conditions. - Dual-System Power Redundancy In conventional battery-swapping trucks, drivers often return for a swap with unused capacity because they are reluctant to run the battery low. Backup power from the range-extension battery increases the main battery’s depth of discharge (DOD) from approximately 70% to over 95%, allowing it to be returned at less than 5% state of charge (SOC). At this threshold, CATL’s seamless switching technology transfers power delivery to the range-extension battery within milliseconds, maintaining a continuous and stable power supply. - “1+X” Architecture and Independent Upgrades The system uses a “1+X” architecture. One standardized main battery maintains compatibility with the QIJI battery-swapping network, while the range-extension battery can be customized for specific conditions with options including ultra-high energy density, low-temperature resistance for cold climates, or ultra-high power. The two battery systems can be developed and upgraded independently to meet their respective technical and operational requirements. - Flexible Leasing and Battery Asset Management The independently owned on-board range-extension battery stays with the vehicle as an asset throughout its service life, reducing reliance on immediate access to a swapping station. The main battery can be leased according to seasonal freight demand, helping fleets reduce rental costs during quieter periods and manage battery assets more flexibly. This architecture combines the benefits of standardization with flexible vehicle configurations, making electric heavy-duty trucks more practical and economically viable across a wider range of applications. QIJI Builds a Shared Battery Swapping Ecosystem QIJI complements these improvements with a three-pillar strategy of standardization, new infrastructure and a full commercial ecosystem. It seeks to speed heavy-duty truck electrification with a value-chain ecosystem co-created by all stakeholders, where benefits are shared collectively. - Standardization Supports Wider Adoption To accommodate a wider range of truck models and operating conditions, QIJI has introduced the 260# (432 kWh) and 300# (513 kWh) standardized battery-swapping blocks alongside the existing 75# block. The system enables battery swaps in just five minutes, with a 99.99% first-time success rate, helping fleets minimize downtime and maintain operational efficiency. QIJI has also pioneered a battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model in which customers pay for the net energy charged rather than the energy discharged. This allows customers to retain the value of energy recovered through regenerative braking, reducing per-kWh battery rental costs for users on basic plans by up to 20%. Flexible battery leasing options allow customers to tailor rental periods to their needs, from second-hand vehicle transitions to seasonal demand. This will minimize idle costs and offer more flexible options for off-season downtime, further helping fleets manage operating costs. - New Infrastructure Improves Resource Efficiency QIJI aims to make better use of four critical resources in long-haul freight: time, land, payload capacity and grid electricity. Rapid battery swapping reduces waiting times, while efficient station layouts serve more vehicles within the same footprint. Battery capacity is matched to transport needs, and centralized, coordinated charging makes better use of grid electricity. These measures aim to improve both resource efficiency and operational returns. CATL plans to deploy 900 battery-swapping stations by the end of 2026 and 2,000 by 2027, with a long-term target of 10,000 stations nationwide in collaboration with its partners. By connecting major freight corridors through a coordinated swapping network, QIJI aims to improve the efficiency and commercial viability of electric heavy-duty trucking. - A Commercial Ecosystem Supports the Full Vehicle Lifecycle QIJI connects truck manufacturers, financial institutions, insurers, channel partners and aftermarket service providers across the vehicle lifecycle, from purchase and operation to maintenance and resale, working together to build a comprehensive ecosystem of integrated products and services. QIJI has introduced two partnership models: Battery Asset Service Partners and Energy Replenishment Service Partners. artigo.texto: O Piauí deu mais um passo para a implantação de sua política de crédito de carbono. Nesta terça-feira (20), foi realizada, no Centro de Educação Ambiental (CEA), em Teresina, a primeira reunião do Conselho Gestor do REDD+(Redução de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa provenientes do Desmatamento e da Degradação Florestal), iniciativa voltada à redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa provenientes do desmatamento e da degradação florestal. O conselho reúne representantes do poder público, da sociedade civil, da academia, dos povos indígenas, das comunidades quilombolas e tradicionais, da agricultura familiar e do setor produtivo. A proposta é garantir participação social, transparência e segurança na construção do projeto, que poderá gerar recursos para a conservação ambiental e beneficiar as populações que contribuem para a proteção das florestas. O secretário do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos, Feliphe Araújo, destacou que a implantação do projeto é uma das prioridades da gestão e ressaltou a importância de construir uma política regulamentada, com participação da sociedade. “Queremos proteger nossas florestas e, ao mesmo tempo, gerar recursos para beneficiar as pessoas que ajudam a preservar o meio ambiente. Por isso, é fundamental que esse processo seja construído com diálogo, transparência e participação de todos os setores”, afirmou. Segundo o secretário, o Estado já avançou na elaboração de normas, na regulamentação da iniciativa e na busca de parceiros para viabilizar o projeto. A experiência de outros estados, como o Tocantins, também serve de referência para acelerar as etapas necessárias à implantação da política no Piauí. Feliphe Araújo ressaltou ainda que a preservação ambiental precisa caminhar junto com o desenvolvimento econômico. Ele citou ações de recuperação de áreas degradadas, educação ambiental, fiscalização e prevenção e combate aos incêndios florestais como medidas complementares para reduzir os impactos ambientais. O modelo de Redução de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa provenientes do Desmatamento e da Degradação Florestal (REDD+) poderá viabilizar mecanismos de pagamento por serviços ambientais, com benefícios para povos indígenas, comunidades quilombolas, populações tradicionais e agricultores familiares, além de contribuir para a conservação dos biomas piauienses. A criação e o funcionamento do conselho representam uma etapa importante para consolidar a governança do projeto, assegurando que as decisões sejam discutidas coletivamente e que a política de crédito de carbono seja construída com responsabilidade ambiental e participação social.

artigo.texto: Chinese energy storage provider Jinko ESS has agreed to supply 34 battery storage systems with a combined capacity of 18 megawatt-hours (MWh) for a telecommunications project in Mali, adding to investment aimed at reducing diesel dependence across Africa’s mobile networks. Announced on 17 October 2026, the agreement covers Jinko ESS’s SunGiga G2 Plus systems. The company, a subsidiary of solar manufacturer Jinko Solar, has not disclosed the project partner, contract value or installation sites. The announcement comes as telecommunications operators and infrastructure providers seek more reliable and cost-effective ways to power network equipment in markets where grid electricity can be inconsistent and fuel delivery expensive. The deal reflects a wider shift in how energy is managed across Africa’s telecommunications sector. Mobile towers require continuous power to maintain voice and data services, including in rural and remote areas where grid connections may be weak or unavailable. Diesel generators have traditionally filled that gap, but their operating costs, maintenance requirements and exposure to fuel supply disruptions have encouraged companies to consider solar generation and battery storage. According to a July 2025 analysis by CrossBoundary Energy, approximately 70% of Africa’s 500,000 telecommunications towers rely on diesel. At remote sites, fuel can account for between 30% and 60% of operating expenditure. The cost of transporting fuel adds further pressure, particularly where sites are difficult to reach or supply routes are disrupted. These expenses can make energy one of the most significant controllable costs in operating a telecommunications network. Battery storage can help address some of these challenges by storing electricity generated from solar panels or drawn from the grid when available, then supplying power when generation falls or the grid fails. In hybrid systems, batteries can reduce the hours diesel generators need to operate, while solar generation can lower the amount of fuel consumed. The extent of the savings depends on local solar resources, electricity demand, battery configuration, generator efficiency and the reliability of existing power infrastructure. Jinko ESS has not disclosed whether the 34 SunGiga G2 Plus systems will be installed alongside new solar capacity, integrated into existing hybrid power systems or deployed as part of a broader network upgrade. Without details on the sites and system configuration, the project’s expected reduction in diesel consumption, operating costs and emissions cannot yet be quantified. The agreement comes amid a series of investments in renewable energy for Mali’s telecommunications infrastructure. In March 2025, the Facility for Energy Inclusion (FEI) and Norfund signed financing agreements totalling US$40 million with Communication and Renewable Energy Infrastructure (CREI), an asset management company specialising in energy infrastructure for telecommunications. The financing supports CREI’s Telecom Energy Service Company model, under which it develops, builds, operates and maintains energy assets for mobile network operators. CREI said the wider investment programme would modernise telecommunications tower infrastructure in Mali through hybrid renewable energy systems incorporating solar and battery storage. The approach allows network operators to obtain energy services without necessarily financing and managing all the underlying power equipment themselves. For providers of distributed energy infrastructure, such arrangements can create opportunities to aggregate sites and deliver energy solutions at scale. Further financing followed in November 2025, when the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the West African Development Bank (BOAD) announced an €80 million financing package for Orange Mali. The investment is intended to support the installation of 300 new 4G towers, expand fibre connectivity and improve access to digital services, particularly in rural areas. As part of the project, Orange Mali is expected to replace diesel generators with solar-powered systems, with the IFC estimating that the change will reduce carbon dioxide emissions by more than 8,000 tonnes annually. These investments demonstrate how energy infrastructure and digital connectivity are increasingly linked. Reliable mobile networks support financial services, education, business transactions and access to information. Where electricity supply is unstable, network operators must invest in backup power and fuel logistics to maintain service. Those costs can affect the commercial viability of expanding coverage into remote communities, where average revenues per user may be lower and infrastructure more expensive to operate. The transition to solar and battery-based systems is therefore not only an emissions issue. It is also a question of network resilience and the economics of extending digital services. Lower fuel consumption can reduce exposure to price volatility and delivery delays, while battery systems can provide a buffer against grid interruptions. However, energy storage introduces its own costs, including equipment procurement, replacement over time, maintenance and the need for appropriate system monitoring. For investors and equipment suppliers, the opportunity lies in delivering solutions that remain reliable under local operating conditions. Telecom sites can differ considerably in electricity demand, climate, security risks and accessibility. Systems installed in remote locations must be designed for limited maintenance access and must maintain performance over years of continuous operation. Procurement price alone will not determine the long-term economics; equipment durability, warranties, service capacity and battery lifecycle costs will also matter. artigo.texto: Doc Brown needed 1.21 gigawatts to send a DeLorean through time in the 1985 movie "Back to the Future." The data-center industry could add about 42 times that next year. Welcome to the Doc Brown Index. Research firm SemiAnalysis expects annual additions to data center IT capacity outside China to more than double next year, to about 51 gigawatts from 25 gigawatts this year. In movie units, that's about 21 Doc Browns ballooning to 42. These are additions in a single year, not the whole fleet or the electricity it uses. By SemiAnalysis's count, that one year would roughly match the world's entire data center build-out through 2024. About three-quarters of next year's projected additions come from projects already operational or under construction. The rest are still planned. SemiAnalysis points to more than 24 gigawatts across 40 campuses in advanced construction for expected delivery next year. Not everyone buys it. At the All-In Summit in September, Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner called SemiAnalysis's forecast at the time, 43 gigawatts, too aggressive and guessed the industry would stand up closer to 25 gigawatts. That's only about 21 Doc Browns — no faster than this year. How do you build that much, that quickly? Increasingly, in pieces. Suppliers now build electrical rooms and cooling systems in factories while crews prepare the site. SemiAnalysis calls the results Lego data centers, with bricks that can weigh 50,000 pounds. Amazon (AMZN) is rolling out its own modular design at large scale, and Meta Platforms (META) has put up tent-like halls to enclose buildings faster, according to SemiAnalysis. A SemiAnalysis model of a 50-megawatt AI data hall puts conventional construction at 22 months and a fully modular approach at 14, excluding permitting. The biggest saving comes from electrical and mechanical installation. For the owner of the chips inside, SemiAnalysis values that eight-month head start at about $200 million. That shift puts suppliers in the race alongside chipmakers such as Nvidia (NVDA). SemiAnalysis estimates content per megawatt for Vertiv (VRT) roughly doubles, to as much as $7 million, when it sells the full modular stack. Contractors Comfort Systems USA (FIX) and Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) assemble modules too. But a finished building still needs power. Microsoft (MSFT) confirmed Monday that it pulled out of a lease at a planned 50-megawatt Nscale data center outside London — the same size as the SemiAnalysis model — after grid officials said power might not arrive until the 2030s. Microsoft said the decision involved a single site and that its broader partnership with Nscale continues.

artigo.texto: VSL PowerHive to Launch 7.5 GWh Battery Storage Facility 19 Oct 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share VSL PowerHive, a wholly owned subsidiary of Vikram Solar, plans to establish a 7.5 GWh per annum Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) assembly facility at Oragadam near Chennai in Tamil Nadu. The plant is scheduled for inauguration in January 2027, with commercial operations expected to begin in April 2027. It will initially cover approximately 165,000 square feet and can be expanded to 15 GWh in subsequent phases. The facility forms part of Vikram Solar’s plan to develop 30 GWh of total battery manufacturing capacity by 2030. The company is also planning a 7.5 GWh battery cell manufacturing programme from 2028, with the aim of creating an integrated domestic ecosystem covering cells and complete energy storage systems. The Oragadam plant will manufacture lithium iron phosphate-based BESS products for utility-scale and commercial and industrial applications. Its planned portfolio includes 5.016 MWh and 6.25 MWh liquid-cooled BESS containers, PowerHive P261 battery cabinets, utility-scale storage systems and renewable energy-integrated storage solutions. The operations will be developed under the Make in India initiative. The expansion comes as India increases its solar and wind power capacity and requires storage to manage renewable power variability, support grid stability and shift surplus electricity to periods of peak demand. Projections from the Central Electricity Authority indicate that the country will require approximately 47 GW of energy storage power capacity and 236 GWh of storage capacity by 2031–32, creating opportunities for domestic manufacturers and reducing dependence on imported technologies. VSL PowerHive is developing indigenous battery technologies and has initiated several patent filings to strengthen its intellectual property portfolio. Vikram Solar chairman and managing director Gyanesh Chaudhary said the facility would extend the company’s clean energy activities beyond solar generation technologies, while chief executive Arun Mittal said the phased expansion would build advanced domestic manufacturing capabilities. The project is also expected to create skilled employment, develop local expertise and support Tamil Nadu’s clean technology manufacturing ecosystem. artigo.texto: Data center opponents are holding a series of eight marches across Virginia to call for a statewide moratorium on their construction. On Monday, they’ll be marching in Danville, which is an interesting choice, since the region is slated to get at least 2,050 jobs over the coming years at a data center complex to be built at the Southern Virginia Megasite. If that number comes to fruition — and that is the number of permanent jobs, not construction jobs, that the performance agreement calls for — it would be the largest jobs announcement in Southside in, well, a long time. The Virginia Economic Development Partnership database goes back to 1990 and the largest is the 2,015 jobs slated for the Microporous battery plant that’s now under construction. It’s unusual to see people marching against jobs in a part of the state that has undergone decades of economic trauma with the loss of key industries. On the other hand, those data center jobs aren’t there yet, but the energy demands from data centers are — something that those in neighboring Pittsylvania County know well since that county has approved more solar projects than any other in the state, according to the Weldon Cooper Center for Public Service at the University of Virginia, and officials there have spoken openly about “solar fatigue.” To that extent, Southside is a good place to examine the tensions and trade-offs with data centers: jobs and tax revenue versus energy requirements. There’s also something of a class conflict at work: Virginia’s most affluent counties in Northern Virginia are now tiring of data centers but some of its poorest counties in rural Virginia see data centers as an opportunity for long-sought revenue. Two counties to the east of Danville is Mecklenburg, which has been able to use revenue from a Microsoft data center complex to build three new schools, something most rural counties can’t afford. Many rural counties see a potential moratorium as a case of the rich telling the poor they can’t have the same opportunities; on the other hand, individual counties aren’t responsible for meeting the state’s energy requirements. State Sen. Russet Perry, D-Loudoun County, whose district includes “Data Center Alley,” last week announced she’ll be introducing a bill to impose a three-year moratorium on data center development. That seems unlikely to become law. In an appearance at the Governor’s Summit on Rural Prosperity in Lexington, Gov. Abigail Spanberger said she’s against a statewide moratorium because some localities want data centers — and those who don’t can impose their own moratoriums at any time. I asked Perry about the implications of her proposed moratorium on the Stack project in Pittsylvania and here’s what she emailed me: “A recent Brookings study found that while data centers do create some jobs, the long-term employment gains are much more modest than industry claims suggest. Beside the questionable jobs numbers being put forward by the wealthiest corporations to ever exist, simultaneously we have depleting water tables and an unstable power grid in Virginia, largely caused by the strains of the data center industry. The people of Southside Virginia, like those across the commonwealth, deserve the security of knowing they will have clean water to drink and can turn on the lights in their homes. Those are resources every family across Virginia depends on.” Meanwhile, from Kevin Hughes of Stack Infrastructure, the developer of that 2,500-job Pittsylvania County project: “A data center moratorium doesn’t eliminate demand for digital infrastructure. It shifts where that infrastructure gets built and where the investment goes. Americans will continue creating data, businesses will continue adopting AI and demand for digital services will only grow. The question is whether we build the infrastructure to support that growth in a given locality, state or even in the United States, or increasingly rely on capacity elsewhere. This is about more than jobs and economic development. It’s about American competitiveness, the resilience of our digital infrastructure, and maintaining greater control over sensitive information. Communities should absolutely have a voice in how infrastructure is developed, and legitimate concerns deserve thoughtful, fact-based solutions. But restricting data center development won’t stop demand. It risks sending investment, innovation and opportunity somewhere else.” Those are the politics of a potential moratorium. What about the technicalities? That’s what I set out to explore today. What would happen if Virginia did impose a statewide moratorium? Or if enough localities imposed their own that much of the state was off-limits to data centers? The answer seems obvious and Hughes’ answer foreshadows it: Data centers would simply go somewhere else. Even without a moratorium, Virginia is on the verge of losing its crown as the world’s data center capital. The commercial real estate firm JLL recently reported that Texas now has almost as much data center capacity as Virginia — and is in the process of building more than we are. We can’t say that Virginia is losing data centers to Texas, but Texas is certainly gaining them at a faster rate now. That might simply be inevitable: Texas is a lot bigger geographically than Virginia so, as the saying goes, everything is bigger in Texas. Some might like a statewide moratorium, some might not. You might see the results of either policy in your power bill or your tax bill, but your experience as a data consumer would not change. You could still swipe your card at the gas pump, you could still upload your funny cat video to TikTok, you could still watch all the Netflix movies you want and never notice which data centers all that data is being routed through. TikTok uses a lot of servers in Virginia now, but until 2023 it stored some of its American data in Singapore. Some of your other online transactions might already be happening on servers overseas

artigo.texto: Swiss-based PowerEdge selects Elisa Industriq’s Gridle for 37 MWh long-duration battery project in Finland The 10 MW / 37 MWh Pelkosenniemi project marks PowerEdge’s entry into utility-scale battery energy storage market in Finland, with Gridle selected as its long-term optimization and trading partner. Swiss-based PowerEdge AG has selected Elisa Industriq’s Gridle as the long-term optimization, trading and route-to-market partner for a 10 MW / 37 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Pelkosenniemi, northern Finland. Gridle will take responsibility for bringing the battery to the electricity market, using AI-powered multi-market optimization and trading to maximize its long-term commercial value. PowerEdge has been responsible for the wider project coordination, structuring and development. The project is majority-owned by renewable energy investment platform Frigg, which has led the financing work. For PowerEdge, the Pelkosenniemi project reflects how the Finnish battery market is evolving, with increasing balancing-market saturation driving BESS projects towards multiple revenue streams. “We do not believe the opportunity in Finland is disappearing, but it is changing. The projects being built for the next market cycle need to capture value from a broader and more volatile set of markets. That is one of the reasons we are focusing on four-hour and potentially even longer-duration storage,” says Anssi Laitinen, CEO and co-founder of PowerEdge. Pelkosenniemi is PowerEdge’s first utility-scale BESS project in Finland and an important step in the company’s plans to build a broader Finnish energy storage portfolio. PowerEdge selected Gridle following an evaluation of optimization capabilities, operational reliability and long-term partnership potential. “For an asset of this size and duration, we needed an optimization partner capable of working across several markets. Gridle’s experience with longer-duration batteries, strong optimization capabilities and ability to adapt the strategy as the Finnish market evolves were key factors in our decision,” says Panu Kärävä, Head of Projects at PowerEdge. With 37 MWh of energy capacity and approximately four hours of storage duration, the battery can combine balancing-market participation with more energy-intensive trading opportunities. “Long-duration batteries require sophisticated optimization as value shifts between balancing and wholesale markets. Having optimized longer-duration batteries for more than five years, we bring expertise that is increasingly valuable for utility-scale BESS investors. We are pleased to support PowerEdge and Frigg in maximizing the long-term value of the Pelkosenniemi investment,” says Markus Logren, Gridle Business Lead at Elisa Industriq. The Pelkosenniemi battery project is currently under construction, with commercial operations expected to begin in early 2027. More information & interview requests: Elisa Industriq Mediadesk, mediadesk@elisaindustriq.com, tel. +358 50 305 1605 PowerEdge, Anssi Laitinen, Co-founder and CEO, contact@poweredge.energy, tel. +41 76 560 5485 About Gridle Gridle helps energy asset owners maximize the long-term value of batteries and other flexible energy assets. Its AI-powered service combines forecasting, multi-market optimization, real-time control, electricity-market trading, settlement and transparent performance reporting. Gridle manages thousands of flexible energy assets and more than 500 MWh of flexible capacity across grid-scale, industrial, telecom and residential applications. Drawing on Elisa’s 140+ years of innovation and automation and its expertise in operating nationally critical infrastructure, Gridle delivers dependable energy services that translates directly into operational efficiency and measurable financial outcomes. elisaindustriq.com/gridle About Elisa Industriq Elisa Industriq creates software solutions for operational intelligence by multiplying industrial knowledge with AI innovation. Our businesses – camLine, sedApta, Polystar, CalcuQuote, TenForce, and Gridle – serve over 2,500 clients internationally in the manufacturing, telecommunications, and energy sectors. Elisa Industriq delivers business value for customers by reducing costs, improving quality, and generating growth. Our software solutions integrate with customers’ existing systems to optimize their operations in areas including manufacturing execution, supply chain optimization, network analytics, and energy management. Elisa Industriq is part of Elisa, a pioneer in telecommunications and digital services headquartered in Finland. Our shared mission is a sustainable future through digitalization. Elisa Industriq employs over 1,500 experts in Europe, Asia, and North America. elisaindustriq.com About PowerEdge PowerEdge AG is a Swiss energy storage and energy infrastructure company active across commercial, industrial and utility-scale battery energy storage. In utility-scale projects, PowerEdge brings together project development, investment, technology, delivery and energy-market partners and coordinates the commercial and technical structure required to move BESS projects from opportunity into execution. The company is currently building a growing portfolio of battery energy storage projects in Finland and other European markets. poweredge.energy About Frigg Frigg is a renewable energy investment and financing platform active in sustainable energy infrastructure. Frigg is the majority investor in the Pelkosenniemi battery energy storage project and has led the financing of the project. frigg.eco

artigo.texto: The Philippines is taking a major step toward building a national carbon market. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered the government to develop a policy framework to guide carbon credit projects, attract investment, and support the country’s climate goals. Under Executive Order No. 127, signed on October 13, 2026, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) will lead the development of the Philippine Carbon Market Policy Framework. The order also creates an inter-agency committee to guide the process and names the DENR as the country’s main authority for carbon markets. The framework will set rules for carbon projects, credit trading, monitoring, and benefit-sharing. It will cover both voluntary carbon markets and international trading under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The DENR must submit the proposed framework to the committee for review and approval within 30 days after the order takes effect. The move could help bring more funding to forest protection, clean energy, farming, and other projects that cut or remove greenhouse gas emissions. However, the detailed rules still need to be developed, and the impact will depend on how the system is put into practice. Marcos Orders National Carbon Market Rules Executive Order No. 127 aims to give the Philippines a clearer and more coordinated approach to carbon markets. The government wants the framework to support climate goals while opening the door to investment, funding, and technology. The EO read: “There is a need to formulate a national carbon market framework aligned with international standards, through a whole-of-government approach, to support the achievement of the country’s NDCs (nationally determined contributions).” Carbon markets allow companies and other buyers to purchase credits from projects that reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions. One carbon credit usually stands for one metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent. These credits are based on specific rules and standards. Selling carbon credits can help fund projects that may struggle to secure enough money through other sources. The new framework will establish rules for: - Which projects qualify, - How credits are issued and transferred, - Accepted carbon standards, and - How projects report results. It will also cover environmental and social safeguards and how project benefits should be shared. These rules could support projects in forestry, renewable energy, agriculture, and other sectors. The order does not create a new carbon tax. Instead, it sets the direction for regulating carbon market activities and developing a more coordinated system for carbon projects. DENR Takes the Lead as Agencies Join Carbon Market Committee The order names the DENR as the national authority for carbon markets. It will oversee eligible projects and help ensure they follow national rules and environmental policies. An Inter-Agency Committee on Carbon Markets (IACCM) will coordinate government policy and review the proposed framework. The Climate Change Commission will chair the committee, while the Department of Finance will serve as vice chair. Other members include: - DENR, Department of Energy, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, Department of Trade and Industry, and the Securities and Exchange Commission. These agencies cover areas that can affect carbon projects, from climate policy and land use to energy, transport, business, and finance. Their cooperation will be important because projects may need several permits and must meet different technical and reporting requirements. The committee will review how the framework is applied. It will also approve fair fees for carbon market applications and certifications. Philippines Plans National Registry to Track Carbon Credits The government will establish a Philippine National Carbon Registry, which the DENR will manage. The digital system is intended to record carbon credits and related transactions. It should help regulators track credits and reduce the risk of the same emissions reduction being counted more than once. This matters when credits are sold to different buyers or transferred between countries. If the same emissions reduction is claimed more than once, the climate benefit becomes less reliable. The framework will also set rules for measuring and checking emissions reductions, approving international transfers, and reporting transactions. These requirements could help buyers assess credits and give project developers a clearer process for selling them in eligible markets. However, the registry’s value will depend on how well the government checks project data, tracks credits, and enforces the rules. Opening the Door to International Carbon Trading The framework will cover both voluntary carbon markets and international trading under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. In voluntary markets, companies and other organizations buy credits to support their climate goals. Eligible projects may include forest conservation, reforestation, renewable energy, farming, and waste management. Article 6 allows countries to work together to meet their climate targets. Under Article 6.2, countries can transfer approved emissions reductions or removals, known as internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs). These transfers require government approval and proper accounting. Countries must follow the rules. This stops the same emissions reduction from counting for more than one climate target. The new framework will set rules for approving international transfers. It will also manage carbon credits. This could help Philippine projects reach international buyers. However, approval under the national framework will not automatically mean that every credit qualifies for every market or buyer. New National Framework Builds on Existing Sector Rules The Philippines is not starting from zero. Several government initiatives have already laid the groundwork for carbon market development. artigo.texto: Neocloud operator Nscale’s IPO plans could be at risk after Microsoft cancels UK data center project British neocloud startup Nscale Global Holdings Ltd.’s plans to launch an initial public offering in the U.S. have suffered a massive setback after its biggest customer Microsoft Corp. pulled out of a critical data center deal this weekend. A report in The Telegraph today said Microsoft has terminated an agreement to rent artificial intelligence infrastructure at the company’s planned facility in Loughton, Essex. The project, which had already been beset by repeated construction delays, has effectively been derailed after U.K. grid officials told Nscale they would not be able to provide adequate power to the site until the 2030s. The cancellation of the deal comes at a time when Nscale is also experiencing construction problems at another facility in Norway. That site has reportedly struggled with cooling system leaks, regulatory hurdles and a fire. A spokesperson for Nscale told The Telegraph that the company’s relationship with Microsoft remains “strong and long-term,” and insisted that the grid issue has no impact on several other contracts it has signed with the Windows software giant. “We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the U.K., and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the U.K.,” the spokesperson said. Nscale announced the facility in September 2025 alongside three other projects as part of a reported $24 billion contract it had signed with Microsoft. The other projects included sites in Texas, Portugal and a second facility in Norway, located close to an existing data center the company already operates. Those projects are all still believed to be on track. However, the future of the Loughton facility is now up in the air. Nscale originally announced plans to install 23,040 Nvidia graphics processing units at the site by the first quarter of 2027, which would have provided an initial 50 megawatts of AI capacity. It also had plans to expand that to 90 megawatts if needed. $MSFT Microsoft has canceled an AI data center deal with Nvidia-backed Nscale in the UK 🤖❌ The facility was expected to house around 23,000 Nvidia GPUs, but electricity may not be available until the 2030s. Other deals between Microsoft and Nscale are not affected. pic.twitter.com/Fmeo7z04Ay — The Future Investors (@ftr_investors) October 18, 2026 The setback comes at a difficult time for Nscale, just a month after the company confidentially filed for an IPO with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It has applied to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol NSCL, and is reportedly hoping to raise $3 billion at a valuation of about $35 billion, well in excess of its private valuation of $15 billion. But with the loss of the Loughton facility, investors are going to be much more skeptical about betting on Nscale. One reason for investors to be nervous is that Microsoft is one of only two major customers Nscale currently has. Microsoft and Anthropic PBC account for approximately 85% of Nscale’s entire contract value, according to its IPO filing. Nscale is one of a number of so-called neoclouds, which are specialized cloud infrastructure providers that rival hyperscalers such as Amazon Web Services Inc., Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. Other well known neoclouds include CoreWeave Inc. in the U.S. and Nebius Group N.V., which has a very strong presence in Europe. They have become popular bets with investors looking to capitalize on the AI boom, but their expansion plans are heavily dependent on being able to secure billions of dollars in funding to construct the data centers and procure the equipment that goes inside them. That leaves them extremely vulnerable should delivery schedules slip or projects end up being canceled. Despite the best efforts of Nvidia Corp., which has tried to create new avenues for Wall Street to fund the AI infrastructure buildout, there have been signs that securing financing has become more difficult. CoreWeave’s stock fell more than 25% last week on concerns about its financing needs. At the weekend, a Financial Times report warned of the growing nervousness investors have over America’s immense AI infrastructure build out, which many believe is propping up the broader U.S. economy. Cracks are appearing in America’s debt-laden $10tn AI infrastructure boom as project delays, public backlash and shaky investor confidence bring a reckoning for the data centre build-out underpinning the US economy https://t.co/UkrO7uUUuO pic.twitter.com/b8kRAMKvXL — Financial Times (@FT) October 18, 2026 Last week, the Australian firm Firmus Technologies Pty. Ltd. abandoned its own IPO plans after failing to attract sufficient demand from prospective investors. In recent weeks, there have been reports that even Oracle Corp. has struggled to finance some of its data center projects. The database giant last month sent a notice of “force majeure” to the developer of its planned facility in New Mexico, following reports that it was also struggling to secure a power source. Against this backdrop, Nscale’s planned IPO is sure to become a real test of investor’s appetite for yet more risky bets whose growth depends on infrastructure that’s still under construction. artigo.texto: BYD Energy Storage Acelera Expansão da Rede Global BESS Pós-Venda AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 20 de outubro de 2026 SHENZHEN, China, Oct. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — A BYD Energy Storage desenvolveu uma rede abrangente de serviços pós-venda em uma estrutura de vários níveis: operação e manutenção de estações, centros de projetos, centros regionais e sede global. A BYD Energy Storage opera nove centros de O&M de 2.500 metros quadrados em todo o mundo. Ela conta com uma rede de serviços de pós-venda em diversos países como China, Chile, África do Sul, Reino Unido, Estados Unidos, Austrália, Japão, Polônia e Oriente Médio. Novos centros de serviços serão inaugurados na África do Sul e na Bulgária em 2027 para expandir ainda mais sua presença global de serviços. Os centros desempenham funções essenciais, como armazenamento e gestão de peças de reposição, reparo e manutenção de baterias, alocação regional de peças de reposição, reciclagem de baterias e treinamento de engenheiros contratados localmente. Os centros regionais da BYD Energy Storage estão em total conformidade com os requisitos regulamentares locais, oferecem treinamento estruturado para a força de trabalho e viabilizam uma resposta local rápida. A equipe de serviços profissionais é composta por mais de 200 engenheiros de campo e mais de 100 especialistas em P&D. A empresa aplica SLAs de serviço padronizados: resposta em até 24 horas, chegada ao local em até 48 horas e solução de problemas em até 7 dias. A rede global de serviços da empresa alcança uma ampla cobertura. Ela forma uma rede de suprimentos multiponto que garante a entrega rápida de peças de reposição em todo o mundo. Além disso, com suas linhas de produção locais, as equipes de operação e manutenção integram recursos regionais para oferecer serviços locais de reparo de baterias, fornecendo aos clientes globais um suporte pós-venda rápido, conveniente e localizado. Nossa presença global de serviços é adaptada às nossas implementações de BESS em rápido crescimento. “O suporte pós-venda confiável sustenta a operação estável de longo prazo dos ativos de armazenamento de energia”, comentou He Dehong, Chefe de Serviço Pós-Venda Global da BYD Energy Storage. Guiado por sua visão de capacitar o setor global de armazenamento de energia com serviços digitais e inteligentes, o sistema global maduro de O&M da BYD Energy Storage apoia fortemente sua crescente presença no armazenamento de energia em baterias. A empresa liderou as remessas globais de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), superando 60 GWh em 2025, e entregou, ao todo, mais de 650 projetos de armazenamento de energia, contando com serviços pós-venda padronizados e localizados que garantem a operação confiável dos ativos. artigo.texto: France-based energy company ENGIE has reached financial close on the 150 MW/300 MWh Hazelwood Battery Energy Storage System expansion (HBESS 2) in Victoria, Australia. The project will increase the site's total battery capacity to 300 MW/450 MWh, including the existing 150 MW/150 MWh system operating since 2023. Located at the former Hazelwood Power Station, the expansion will use existing infrastructure to store electricity, including daytime solar generation, for dispatch during higher-demand periods. Sungrow will supply battery technology, while Elecnor will undertake balance-of-plant and associated infrastructure works. The project follows the site's coal power station closure in 2017 and comes ahead of the planned Yallourn Power Station closure. Construction is scheduled to begin in late 2026, with commercial operations targeted for 2028. artigo.texto: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) drives new technological opportunities, but also increases pressure on natural resources. Data centers that enable model training and query processing require large amounts of electricity, water, and specialized equipment, whose impacts depend on the conditions of each facility. Although computer systems improve their energy efficiency, the increase in users and high-consumption applications can counteract these advances. According to estimates by Our World in Data, AI-dedicated data centers consumed around 0.5% of the world’s electricity in 2025 and could reach 1.5% by 2030. However, calculating the real impact remains complex. The location of facilities, the energy sources used, cooling technologies, and the lack of detailed public information make it difficult to establish a complete assessment of the environmental consequences of this industry. The risks of AI use for the environment One of the main challenges is electricity consumption. Although a text query may require relatively little energy, more demanding tasks, such as generating videos, demand much more computing resources. If the electricity comes from coal or natural gas, its use generates emissions that contribute to global warming. Additionally, some data centers resort to gas turbines and their own generators to ensure supply. These equipment can emit atmospheric pollutants, such as nitrogen oxides and fine particles, which deteriorate air quality and pose health risks to nearby communities. Water is another major concern, as it is used to cool equipment and also during electricity generation. An analysis published in March by scientists from the University of California in Riverside and other institutions estimated that U.S. data centers could consume up to 416 billion liters annually by 2030. The impact may be greater in regions already suffering from water scarcity. Noise, heat, and mineral extraction Local effects also include noise pollution caused by fans, cooling systems, and generators. In certain communities, persistent noise has led to complaints about its effects on quality of life. Furthermore, the heat released by these facilities could intensify urban heat islands. Research conducted in Phoenix, Arizona, detected temperature increases of up to 2.2 °C in neighborhoods downwind of some data centers, although more studies are needed to determine the extent of this phenomenon. On the other hand, IT infrastructure depends on minerals and metals used in semiconductors, servers, and storage systems. Their extraction can cause deforestation, water pollution, and emissions, while equipment replacement increases electronic waste, of which only about one-fifth is recycled globally. How to reduce the ecological footprint of artificial intelligence Experts point out that these impacts can be reduced through planning, regulation, and design decisions. Priority measures include supplying data centers with renewable energies, improving cooling efficiency, and avoiding installations in water-stressed areas. It is also essential to demand transparency about energy consumption, emissions, water use, and the origin of materials. In turn, extending the lifespan of equipment and recovering its components can reduce pressure on ecosystems. Finally, before authorizing new projects, it is necessary to evaluate their economic and social benefits against the local environmental costs. The challenge is to harness the capabilities of AI without transferring its impacts to communities or compromising the resources that future generations will need.

artigo.texto: A Microsoft confirmou esta segunda-feira que se retirou de um acordo com a startup britânica Nscale relativo a um centro de dados dedicado à inteligência artificial (IA) no Reino Unido, atrasando as ambições britânicas no setor. A tecnológica norte-americana tinha acordado, no ano passado, alugar capacidade de computação à Nscale, um fornecedor de infraestruturas de IA apoiado por chips Nvidia, num centro de dados previsto para Loughton, a nordeste de Londres. Um porta-voz da Microsoft indicou, numa declaração enviada à AFP, que a “decisão dizia respeito a um único local” e que a empresa “continuava empenhada na sua parceria com a Nscale”. O acordo tinha sido anunciado em simultâneo com um investimento de vários milhares de milhões de dólares por parte de gigantes tecnológicos norte-americanos, durante a visita de Estado do Presidente Donald Trump no ano passado, que deveria contribuir para tornar o Reino Unido uma superpotência no domínio da inteligência artificial. O antigo primeiro-ministro Keir Starmer tinha descrito o local de Loughton como “o maior centro de dados de IA soberano do Reino Unido”. No entanto, alguns projetos de centros de dados têm dificuldade em avançar devido a preocupações relacionadas com o elevado custo da eletricidade e aos longos prazos de espera para a ligação à rede elétrica britânica. “Continuamos empenhados tanto no projeto de Loughton como no Reino Unido, e estamos a explorar fontes alternativas de energia elétrica para o local, bem como outros locais de expansão no Reino Unido”, afirmou esta segunda-feira um porta-voz da Nscale. “A nossa relação com a Microsoft continua sólida e de longo prazo, e este infeliz problema na rede londrina não tem qualquer impacto nos nossos outros contratos”, acrescentou a mesma fonte. Os meios de comunicação britânicos noticiaram que a distribuidora de eletricidade britânica responsável pela região, a UK Power Networks, tinha informado a Nscale de que o local de Loughton não teria acesso à eletricidade antes da década de 2030. Esta evolução surge num momento em que a Nscale se prepara para uma Oferta Pública Inicial em Nova Iorque, com uma valorização que poderá atingir os 35 mil milhões de dólares, segundo vários meios de comunicação. No seu dossiê para a Oferta Pública, a Nscale sublinhou que “uma parte substancial das [suas] receitas contratuais provinha de um número limitado de clientes com grandes contratos”, nomeadamente a Microsoft e a Anthropic. O acordo de Loughton representava apenas uma pequena parte dos contratos celebrados entre a Microsoft e a Nscale, precisou à AFP uma fonte próxima do processo. No início deste ano, a OpenAI, criadora do ChatGPT, retirou-se de uma parceria com a Nscale e a Nvidia que visava estabelecer uma versão britânica da iniciativa norte-americana Stargate, prevendo investimentos de grande envergadura em infraestruturas de IA.

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia O Tianneng Holding Group revelou seu portfólio de baterias multiquímicas em sua Global Alliance Partner Conference 2026 (Conferência Global de Parceiros da Aliança 2026) em Huzhou 20 de outubro de 2026, às 07:27 HUZHOU, China, 20 de outubro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ — O Tianneng Holding Group revelou seu portfólio de baterias multiquímicas em sua Global Alliance Partner Conference 2026 (Conferência Global de Parceiros da Aliança 2026) em Huzhou, Zhejiang, sob o tema “Liderando o Benefício Ecológico”, reunindo aproximadamente 300 parceiros de todo o mundo. O portfólio abrange quatro vertentes de tecnologia de baterias — chumbo-ácido, íons-lítio, íons-sódio e estado sólido — para aplicações que incluem veículos elétricos de duas e três rodas, veículos de baixa velocidade, força motriz industrial e armazenamento de energia para residências, data centers voltados a IA, usuários comerciais e industriais, além de projetos em escala de concessionária. Parceiros da Argélia, Indonésia, Nigéria, Camboja e Brasil participaram de uma mesa redonda sobre produção local, eletrificação de veículos de duas rodas, armazenamento de energia e transformação da distribuição, concordando que as raízes locais e a sinergia do ecossistema são essenciais. Mi Yue, secretária-geral da New Energy Industry Association for Asia and the Pacific (NEIAAP, Associação da Indústria de Novas Energias para a Ásia e o Pacífico), incentivou a inovação, o reconhecimento mútuo de normas e a colaboração transfronteiriça na cadeia de suprimentos. Guo Kuilong, secretário-geral da Câmara de Comércio da China para Importação e Exportação de Máquinas e Produtos Eletrônicos (CCCME), afirmou que a câmara utilizará sua plataforma para ajudar empresas de novas energias em sua expansão global e promover a cooperação na cadeia industrial para um crescimento mutuamente benéfico. “A incerteza torna os pilares da certeza ainda mais vitais”, disse Zhang Tianren, presidente do Tianneng Holding Group. “O Tianneng Group se concentrará em baterias melhores e soluções de sistema mais abrangentes, impulsionando a pesquisa e o desenvolvimento, a fabricação local e o fortalecimento da marca para construir uma cadeia de suprimentos verde, resiliente e localizada, com parceiros globais.” Sobre o Tianneng Group Fundado em 1986, o Tianneng Group é líder global em soluções de energia verde, impulsionando a inovação em energia para mobilidade elétrica, sistemas de armazenamento de energia e economia circular. Com 21 bases de produção inteligentes, a empresa oferece valor sustentável a mais de 100 países e regiões.
