artigo.texto: WETEX 2026 showcases battery breakthroughs and water technologies in Dubai DUBAI — The 28th edition of the Water, Energy, Technology and Environment Exhibition (WETEX) opens on Tuesday at Dubai World Trade Centre, bringing together international companies and industry specialists to showcase technologies aimed at addressing energy, water management and sustainability challenges. Running from October 20 to 22, the exhibition is organised by Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) and serves as a platform for businesses, investors and decision-makers to explore emerging technologies, partnerships and commercial opportunities across regional and global markets. Battery technology takes centre stage German company ALGATEC is presenting a new battery technology that it says can achieve an energy density of up to 1,000 watt-hours per kilogram. The company describes the technology as a cost-effective alternative to conventional systems, manufactured without lithium or rare earth elements. ALGATEC says the technology is designed to address challenges including volatile supply chains and rising raw material costs. The company has also outlined plans for a dedicated gigafactory to support large-scale industrial production. The performance and commercial viability of the technology will be important considerations as it moves towards potential wider deployment. Packaging business unveils new UAE brand The exhibition is also providing a platform for the Abdul Wahid Al Rostamani Group to introduce VerraPak, the new brand replacing its Sinyou packaging business in the UAE. The company says VerraPak will combine local manufacturing, technical expertise, advanced printing and customisation capabilities to develop packaging tailored to customers’ products and operational requirements. Its approach also emphasises responsible practices and closer collaboration with clients. Huda Al Rostamani, chief commercial projects officer at the group, said the launch reflected growth opportunities in the packaging business, supported by demand from the UAE’s food, hospitality and consumer goods sectors for quality, consistent and environmentally responsible solutions. Water treatment technologies target efficiency Japanese company Toray is showcasing technologies including reverse osmosis, ultrafiltration and membrane bioreactors, with a focus on reliable and efficient water treatment and resource management. Takashi Kurai, president of Toray Membrane Middle East, said the exhibition provides an opportunity to engage with utilities, municipalities, government entities, consultants, contractors and property developers. The company expects these discussions to support potential partnerships and expansion across regional markets. Chinese manufacturers are also presenting filtration and purification systems for residential, commercial and industrial applications. Anhui Chero Technology is highlighting sediment and activated-carbon filter cartridges, reverse-osmosis membrane housings and customised filtration solutions designed to improve water quality and system performance. Fumatech Technology is showcasing membrane technologies for sustainable water treatment, including reverse osmosis, nanofiltration and ultrafiltration, alongside desalination, ultrapure water production and systems designed to minimise liquid waste through water recycling. Regional demand drives commercial opportunities WETEX brings together technologies across water, energy, environmental sustainability, digital transformation and green development. DEWA reported that the 2025 edition attracted more than 50,000 visitors and 3,100 exhibitors, highlighting the event’s role in connecting international suppliers with regional buyers and public-sector organisations.

artigo.texto: Taunton City Council unanimously approves data center ban TAUNTON, Mass. (WJAR) — The Taunton City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to ban data centers amid discussion of a proposed facility at an industrial park in the city. City Hall was packed as opponents turned out for the vote, with residents raising concerns about potential environmental impacts and strain on the local power grid. “I found out, like most people via Facebook, because I wasn’t given a letter,” said Taunton resident Willembert VanBruniswaardt. He also accused data center companies of misconduct. “We’ve seen these data center companies perform all kinds of, frankly, criminal actions. I’m not going to sugarcoat it,” he said. In a letter to Mayor Shaunna O’Connell, property owner VMD Industrial requested an exception to the ban. Asked about the property owner’s warning that the decision could cost it a multimillion-dollar deal, O’Connell said business development must be balanced with residents’ needs. “We always support business, but it has to be done the right way,” she told NBC 10 News. “I know the priority of the council and my priority is to protect the resources that our residents rely on every single day.” The Planning Board said Tuesday night that the John Hancock Road property did not qualify for an exception because no permit application was pending. City leaders said the proposed facility could not be grandfathered in without an existing application. “I’m glad people were here tonight to hear the actual facts, because when people believe the gossip and, you know, crap that’s on Facebook or whatever social media, it starts problems,” O’Connell said. Officials said the ban has no expiration date and would remain in place unless changed through another zoning hearing. - ALSO READ: One year after near-fatal stabbing, Former Fall River Mayor William Flanagan eyes 2027 run The council also approved a moratorium, which officials said would provide additional legal protection if the ban is challenged. Despite the unanimous vote, VanBruniswaardt remained cautious. “I would not describe this as a win. I would describe this as we scored a goal. But there’s still an hour left in the match,” he said. “If someone really wants a data center here, they are going to pour everything they have into it.”

artigo.texto: Trending When a city plans something big, it should not check driver’s licenses at the door. That is what happened Monday night in Woodward. The City Council cancelled its regular meeting and instead held what it called a "community conversation” in the Woodward-Granger High School auditorium. The notice required attendees to show a photo ID with a Woodward address or a piece of mail with their name and Woodward address before they could enter. Security officers and police were there to oversee the screening of IDs. I was there as president of the Iowa Freedom of Information Council and was turned away. So was a rural Dallas County resident interested in data centers. A KCCI reporter saw at least two others who were refused entry. Inside, Mayor Todd Folkerts and three Microsoft officials announced that the company had closed on the purchase of about 600 acres in the Woodward Eco Business Park, on the city’s south side, for a data center campus. About 200 residents listened for 90 minutes. Folkerts said the council would need to approve a development agreement and a site plan before the project could proceed. Fewer than a majority of the five council members attended, so the gathering likely falls outside Iowa’s open meetings law. Legal or not, the residency screening was a mistake. It treated a regional decision as a private family matter. Consider what a data center brings. Microsoft’s representatives told the crowd a closed-loop cooling system would spare the city’s water supply and buying electricity from a wholesaler would protect residential rates. Those are promises about water and electricity, and neither resource stops at a city limit. New power lines would cross farm fields. Construction trucks would use county roads. Storm water runs downhill without regard to annexation maps or city boundaries. A farm family just outside town will live with the data center's lights, noise and traffic as surely as any resident of Main Street. That farm family pays property taxes, too -- just not to the City of Woodward. Iowa law already recognizes that a city’s choices reach past its borders. Section 354.9 of the Iowa Code allows a city to review subdivision plats as far as two miles beyond its city limits, giving the city a voice over how its rural neighbors’ land is developed. On October 12, Woodward denied those same neighbors a seat in the auditorium. The venue underscored that point. Woodward-Granger High School belongs to the Woodward-Granger Community School District, which has its central offices in Granger and reaches into Dallas, Boone and Polk counties. Taxpayers in Granger and the surrounding countryside helped pay for that auditorium. The city used the school district's building and then told people without a Woodward address to stay outside. Iowa’s local governments cooperate all the time. Chapter 28E of the Iowa Code allows cities, counties and other public bodies to share services and work together for mutual advantage. The Legislature has directed the courts to interpret that law liberally. Twelve central Iowa cities, utilities and water districts, including the Xenia Rural Water District, formed Central Iowa Water Works under a 28E agreement to plan the region’s drinking water together. Metro Waste Authority grew out of a 28E agreement among Des Moines-area governments dating to 1969. Polk County and its cities fund emergency management jointly through another 28E agreement. None of these partnerships asks a neighbor for proof of address before letting the person listen to a discussion of matters of mutual concern. A residents-only rule divides communities. It turns the city limit into a wall, as if the people on the far side have no stake in what happens on the near side. This also invites the same treatment in return. If Granger, Madrid or Dallas County someday puts a landfill on Woodward’s doorstep, Woodward residents will want to attend meetings where such a development is discussed. They should get in. Everyone else should, too. Monday’s rule was also unneighborly. Picture a farmer who plans a hog confinement on his fence line and invites only his own household to hear the details. The people downwind would not call that a community conversation. They would call it a snub. I told KCCI the requirement that only Woodward residents could attend Monday's information session “erodes the trust and confidence” in Woodward city government. And the damage spreads beyond Woodward. Woodward still has time to fix this. The development agreement and site plan still need council approval. The council will have to take these up at regular, properly noticed meetings that are open to anyone who wants to attend. Woodward officials should invite the Dallas County Board of Supervisors, the Woodward-Granger school board and nearby townships to hear the plan. It should publish what Microsoft has said about water, power and traffic. Woodward’s neighbors will live with this data center. They deserve to hear about it, ask about it and argue about it in the same room as everyone else. A project this large deserves the widest audience -- not the narrowest. Randy Evans is the executive director of the Iowa Freedom of Information Council. He can be reached at DMREvans2810@gmail.com.

artigo.texto: Why Should Delaware Care? Government works best when its citizens are knowledgeable and engaged. Delaware’s government has scores of commissions, working groups, agencies and legislative committees. All must hold meetings that are open to the public. Below we highlight a few of those meetings that are happening this week. Below you will find information about the most important or interesting public meetings happening in Delaware this week. - Hospital cost review board to discuss charity care - State opioid commission to review grants for approval - Wilmington to host an early season budget town hall - Sussex County to consider a slate of new solar fields - Harrington to discuss a data center ban Will hospitals become more charitable? Delaware’s controversial hospital oversight board will meet Tuesday morning to discuss a new law that goes into effect early next year, compelling hospitals to widen the net of patients eligible for free or discounted care. The Diamond State Hospital Cost Review Board is set to discuss regulations that will guide how hospitals will be held accountable for the new codified standards in the years to come. The law requires hospitals to expand eligibility for free and discounted care, usually called charity care. In order to qualify for their tax-exempt nonprofit status, hospitals must offer a “community benefit,” according to the IRS. Historically, that benefit has been charity care. Earlier this month, financial leaders from Delaware’s hospital systems flooded a small government meeting room to voice concerns with the drafted regulations. The regulations are also being crafted with input from the state’s hospital lobbying group, the Delaware Healthcare Association, which expressed support for the legislation but asked state leaders to target other healthcare sectors that also earn money from patients, such as insurers and pharmaceutical companies. 📍 The Diamond State Hospital Cost Review Board is set to meet at 10 a.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 20, at the Herman M. Holloway Sr. Campus – DHSS Chapel, located at 1901 N. Dupont Highway in New Castle. More information, including about virtual attendance, can be found here. State to approve new opioid dollars The Delaware commission charged with appropriating dollars secured from state settlements with opioid manufacturers and distributors will meet Monday to review grant applications submitted by local governments and nonprofits. The meeting comes a year after lawmakers reformed how the commission grants dollars to organizations. Those reforms followed reports of mismanagement and potential fraud within the program that emerged the previous year. The Delaware Opioid Settlement Commission is expected to receive $250 million from opioid settlements through 2038. Spotlight Delaware previously reported that Delaware has the only state government that directly distributes money from opioid settlements to various organizations, rather than leaving it up to counties, cities, and towns. 📍 The Delaware Opioid Settlement Commission will meet Monday from 1 to 3 p.m. at the Springer Building, located at 203 Mitchell Lane, in New Castle. For information about virtual attendance and other meeting details, click here. Wilmington to get a head start on its budget The Wilmington City Council on Tuesday will host its first budget town hall as part of an early start to next year’s budget negotiations. Last week, the council announced plans to hold four town halls covering the city’s eight districts, giving residents an opportunity to learn about the budget process, discuss financial priorities or concerns and raise questions. The town halls come after a budget season earlier this year that was marked by debate between the mayor and City Council over how to address housing needs in the city. The city did not hold similar public meetings early in the process last year. 📍 Wilmington’s first-of-four budget town halls is scheduled for Tuesday from 6 to 7 p.m. at the NOMA Library, located at 3905 North Market Street in Wilmington. For more information, click here. Solar fields in Sussex County The Sussex County Council on Tuesday will consider plans for four solar fields – two in Seaford, one in Laurel and one in Delmar. Together they would cover almost 170 acres of farmland, equal to over 100 football fields. They would also have the capacity to produce 11 megawatts of electricity, enough to power about 9,000 homes. The proposals come as Gov. Matt Meyer has encouraged solar development as a way to produce more power in the state. Earlier this year, he fast-tracked permits for some solar projects. He also signed a bill that guarantees power bill discounts for those who sign up for community solar projects. At the same time, some residents feel the arrays are covering too much farmland and could harm local ecosystems. The county’s Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval for all the proposals. 📍 The Sussex County Council will meet Tuesday at 1 p.m. at the Sussex County Administrative Office Building, located at 2 The Circle in Georgetown. The public hearings for the solar projects will begin at 1:30 p.m. For additional details, including information about virtual attendance, click here. Harrington data center ban Harrington on Monday will do a first reading of an ordinance that would ban any data center projects within its borders. The city council recently rejected a proposal to build a data center on the site of a former cold storage warehouse. Residents packed into the meeting room for the vote, overwhelmingly in opposition to the plan. That opposition came despite the developer behind the proposal offering the city of about 4,000 people contributions totaling $1 million. The council will hold its official hearing for the ordinance at a later date, but Monday’s meeting will be the first time the ordinance will be publicly discussed. 📍 Harrington City Council will meet Monday at 6 p.m. at the Harrington Public Library, located at 101

artigo.texto: We have spotted what appears to be a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) for the BYD Flash Charger at Denza Glenmarie in Shah Alam. If our observation is accurate, Denza Glenmarie, which is operated by Sisma Auto, could very well be the location of the first BYD Flash Charger in Malaysia. Why are the BESS units a dead giveaway? Even though the charger’s signature T-shaped structure that houses the charging connectors has not yet been installed at the site, the hardware that we spotted at Denza Glenmarie visually aligns with the BYD Flash Charge energy storage enclosures that we have seen in China. Back in May, Managing Director of BYD Malaysia, Jacob Ma, revealed that Denza showrooms would be among the very first locations to receive BYD Flash Charge stations. He has also confirmed that the BYD Flash Charger will be open to EVs from all brands, rather than being exclusive to BYD and Denza vehicles. BYD Flash Charge can deliver up to 1.5MW, supported by BESS Introduced globally earlier this year, BYD Flash Charge stations are capable of hitting a peak DC charging rate of up to 1.5MW (1,500kW). With supported vehicles, here’s how the charging duration would be: - 10-70% in 5 minutes - 10-97% in 9 minutes - Add 3 more minutes if the temperature is cold Hence, BYD has come up with a tagline for the Flash Charging technology to represent the speed: “Ready in 5, Full in 9, Cold Add 3,”. In order to support the ultra-high power demand and overcome grid limitations, BYD has integrated BESS into the Flash Charge station. These battery banks are being charged from the local grid during idle periods and unleash massive power bursts when a compatible EV plugs in. The battery in each cabinet has a capacity of 185kWh, so you are looking at a 370kWh total battery capacity for each Flash Charger. When required, the BESS draw energy from the grid at speed of between 100kW to 560kW, depending on the infrastructure capability. Meanwhile, Flash Charge’s T-shaped pillar doubles as a “Zero Gravity” cable management system. The charging cables are suspended from the top to ensure that the cables remain clean and off the ground at all times. Not to forget, they can also slide from left to right to accommodate EVs with either left- or right-mounted charging ports. Which BYD models in Malaysia can support Flash Charging? To hit a DC charging speed of 1,500kW, the EV must support BYD’s 1,000V platform and be equipped with the 2nd generation BYD Blade battery. Currently, the only BYD model in Malaysia that can fully support Flash Charge is the Denza Z9 GT, which was launched here back in July. However, non-BYD EVs or older 400V/800V BYD models can still plug in and charge at their maximum supported DC intake rate. As Jacob Ma previously explained, an 800V EV capable of taking 220kW DC will draw 220kW at a BYD Flash Charger. If an 800V vehicle supports up to 600kW, the Flash Charger will supply the full 600kW without issue.

artigo.texto: FAYETTEVILLE, N.C. (WTVD) -- The future of a proposed data center in Fayetteville remains uncertain after a special City Council session Monday morning drew a crowd of concerned residents demanding transparency and answers. Dozens filled the council chamber, some holding signs reading "Moratorium now, do the right thing," as city leaders debated next steps for a project that has been the subject of heated discussion in the community for the past eight months. After nearly two hours, the council scheduled another public hearing to further discuss the draft moratorium and agreed to consult an attorney to revise the proposed ordinance language, leaving many attendees frustrated by the lack of clear resolution. "They're flying the plane while they're building it," said Christi Davis, an Eastover resident who lives just 1.1 miles from a proposed data center site. "The deal, it's got to go through a bunch of hoops to get passed. But Fayetteville, if the landowner requests annexation, then Fayetteville's rules apply. Right now, Cumberland County's rules apply, and it's agricultural land at the moment." The council's deliberations come after a 120-day study, launched in April, which included tours of data centers in North Carolina and Virginia and consultations with industry experts. According to city officials, three community sessions have been held, with water use, noise, and power emerging as residents' top concerns. Councilmember Shaun McMillan voiced frustration about the lack of preparedness and transparency: "I would love to understand why we didn't have the advanced materials both in text and in PowerPoint form prior to this meeting," he said. Despite a lengthy presentation, many residents left the meeting feeling their questions had gone unanswered. Nubian "King" Holmes, a Fayetteville resident, said, "They were unprepared, nor did they have answers to simple yes or no questions. How do you vote on something like that? There are too many things at stake. There are too many people's livelihood and health at risk." Davis echoed the sentiment, expressing dissatisfaction with the council's approach. "They should have gone on and voted the moratorium because all this stuff is taking time and they're seeing it. And this they can't even agree," she said. "They're jumping the gun. They're flying the plane while they're building it. And that's why we need the moratorium to give us time to set this stuff in motion." The City Council plans to draft a moratorium ahead of its next work session, scheduled for November. The conversation is far from over as residents and officials continue to debate the project's effects and the city's path forward.

artigo.texto: It was deju vu all over again on Tuesday night when the Little Rock City Board of Directors failed on a 4-4 vote to pass a six-month moratorium on data center projects. The board took up this issue in August, when some members tried to pass an 18-month moratorium. But the board made the same vote, with the same directors voting the same way. Six votes are needed to pass an ordinance. The ordinance being considered Tuesday would have given the city time to set up restrictions and regulations relating to water, noise, emergency infrastructure, zoning regulations and monitoring relating to data center projects. The urgency to pass an ordinance comes at a time when Google is planning to build a $1 billion data center at the Port of Little Rock. Both measures were sponsored by Director Kathy Webb, and at both meetings, Jay Chesshir, head of the Little Rock Regional Chamber, came in like a relief pitcher to finish the deal, appearing to scare away anyone considering voting with the “yes” contingent with threats that a moratorium could mean legal trouble for the city. One of the “no” votes came from Webb’s friend, Director Capi Peck, who was listed in the agenda handout as a co-sponsor of the moratorium ordinance. After Peck voted against Webb’s 18-month moratorium back in August, she took heat on social media for her action. Webb seemed to be expecting a different outcome this week. In a text exchange earlier in the day, she was asked if she thought the measure would pass. “I think so!” she wrote back. “Four sponsors including me.” After the meeting, Webb said the vote caught her by surprise. “It was a shock,” she said. “It was not expected.” She said she thought she had five votes going into the meeting and was hoping to peel off one of the at-large directors. Asked if she was done with trying to get a moratorium passed, she said possibly, but that she had made a promise when the board passed an ordinance regulating data centers in June to make improvements to that measure. “I keep my promises,” she said. A half-dozen citizens spoke in support of the passage of the ordinance, with one person speaking against it. Then came time for the directors to speak. Peck confirmed she was a co-sponsor – giving Webb credit for the lion’s share of the work – and said she had read over the measure and marked it up several times. In the end, though, she said she still found it to be “pretty technical.” She then invited Brad Jordan, director of Planning and Development for the city, to the microphone, asking him if his department could handle everything that would be required to implement the ordinance. “Whatever we’re asked to do, we’ll do it and we’ll do it well,” he said. He went on to say that getting it done in such a short period of time would be challenging. “It means for the next year, we’ll be doing this,” he said. Director Dean Kumpurus, instead of immediately giving his thoughts, invited Chesshir to speak, a move that brought a few grumbles from the crowded chamber. Chesshir also spoke against the 18-month moratorium. Chesshir’s main argument was that most of what was covered in Webb’s legislation would already be dealt with by one of several local, state or federal agencies, such as the state health department and the Arkansas Division of Environmental Quality, as well as the federal Environmental Protection Agency. To pass an ordinance that conflicts with those agencies would be to invite “legal and litigation risk,” Chesshir said. In all, Directors B.J. Wyrick, Virgil Miller Jr. and Andrea Lewis joined Webb in voting for the measure, while Directors Lance Hines, Kumpuris and Joan Adcock joined Peck in voting against it. Director Antwan Phillips abstained.

artigo.texto: Huawei automotive unit joins CATL network with 2,520 stations — Electrek In China, Huawei’s automotive unit Yinwang, also known as Newcool, has entered into a framework agreement on strategic cooperation with battery manufacturer CATL and its subsidiary CAES. The agreement provides for the use of swappable batteries and vehicle compatibility with CATL’s Choco-swap network, which has 2,520 stations in around 200 Chinese cities. As Electrek reports, CATL plans to adapt vehicles with Huawei’s Qiankun intelligent driving systems for Choco-swap stations. The company wants to connect the vehicle, station and cloud services so that the system determines a car’s energy needs based on battery condition and driver habits, finds a station and independently directs the vehicle for a battery swap. Battery swap in 99 seconds According to CATL, the battery swap itself at a station can take 99 seconds. CATL Chairman Robin Zeng and Huawei Senior Vice President and Yinwang CEO Jin Yuzhi took part in signing the agreement. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram. Huawei owns 80% of Yinwang, while Seres and Changan-affiliated Avatr hold 10% each. Seres produces premium SUVs under the AITO brand, while Qiankun systems are also used by other Chinese automakers. Expansion of the Choco-swap network CATL entered the battery-swapping market in 2022 with the EVOGO service and relaunched this business under the Choco-swap brand with standardized battery packs at the end of 2024. At the end of 2025, the network had 1,020 stations; in early July, the number exceeded 2,000, and as of September 29, it reached 2,520. CATL is building more than 200 battery-swap stations per month and aims to increase their number to more than 3,000 by the end of the year. Other network partners include GAC, BAIC and NIO. At the same time, the agreement with Yinwang is a framework agreement: specific vehicle models, launch timelines and service regions have not been announced.

artigo.texto: Hitachi Global Life Solutions (Hitachi GLS) will begin accepting orders for its AIXROSS air-cooled chiller units for data centers in April 2027. The new system is designed to address increasing server density and heat generation associated with generative AI, combining cooling capacity with energy efficiency. It also aims to reduce water consumption, support stable operation, and accommodate future cooling infrastructure expansion. AIXROSS will be available in a 2450 model with a rated cooling capacity of 245 kW (approximately 836,000 BTU/h), based on planned specifications. The lineup includes a standard version without refrigerant pumps, a Hybrid-M version with one refrigerant pump, and a Hybrid-H version with two refrigerant pumps. Each configuration is available with or without an integrated chilled-water circulation pump. The rated capacity is specified at an outdoor air temperature of 40°C (104°F), chilled-water inlet temperature of 30°C (86°F), and outlet temperature of 20°C (68°F). The newly designed refrigeration cycle improves cooling capacity and coefficient of performance (COP) at outdoor temperatures of 40°C (104°F). Hybrid configurations automatically switch between compressor and refrigerant pump cycles according to ambient temperature and operating conditions, with the aim of reducing electricity consumption during low-temperature operation. Hitachi GLS expects these features to contribute to lower annual energy consumption. For installation flexibility, AIXROSS supports bottom air intake to reduce space requirements. Hitachi GLS also offers engineering services covering modular configurations that integrate chillers with piping, pumps, tanks, and other peripheral equipment. A high-speed startup mode reduces the time required to return to rated-capacity operation following a power outage. Integrated chilled-water pumps can also be connected to an external uninterruptible power supply (UPS). The modular system adjusts the number of operating modules according to thermal load, supporting stable operation under low-load conditions. AIXROSS supports remote monitoring through Hitachi GLS’s exiida HVAC IoT solution, which requires a separate paid contract. The company also plans to introduce predictive fault detection and energy-saving controls using physical AI. The chiller will form part of Hitachi’s HMAX Data Center solution portfolio, which integrates AI-based operation, maintenance, and optimization across data center power, IT, and cooling infrastructure.

artigo.texto: Avaliação de Data Center de IA do Condado de Grant Expõe uma Lacuna de Relatórios de Nove Dígitos O Condado de Grant descobriu mudanças não reportadas em propriedades de data centers de IA, incluindo uma ampliação estimada em mais de US$ 100 milhões. A avaliação de data center de IA do Condado de Grant agora levanta uma questão básica: os registros tributários locais conseguem acompanhar campi computacionais cada vez mais complexos? A descoberta não estabelece automaticamente fraude tributária, ocultação deliberada ou um valor final de impostos não pagos. As informações publicamente disponíveis ainda não resolveram esses pontos. Elas mostram, porém, que mudanças físicas importantes estavam ausentes das informações usadas pelos avaliadores locais. Essa distinção importa em Quincy, Washington, onde Microsoft e diversos operadores de colocation construíram grandes campi em torno de energia hidrelétrica barata e acesso à fibra óptica. Os data centers se tornaram centrais para a base tributária local, tornando registros imobiliários precisos mais do que uma questão administrativa. O Condado de Grant agora precisa determinar quando cada melhoria passou a ser tributável, como ela deve ser avaliada e se avaliações anteriores exigem correção. Os operadores podem contestar essas decisões, como vários proprietários de data centers de Quincy já fizeram antes. Portanto, o conflito é maior do que uma estrutura negligenciada. A infraestrutura de IA está se expandindo mais rapidamente, tornando-se mais densa e incorporando equipamentos mais especializados. Os sistemas locais de avaliação ainda dependem de licenças, declarações dos proprietários, inspeções físicas e comunicação precisa entre departamentos. O Que Encontrou a Avaliação de Data Center de IA do Condado de Grant A principal constatação é uma lacuna de relatórios, e não ainda uma decisão tributária final. Segundo a investigação local inicial, autoridades do condado identificaram mudanças em data centers que não haviam sido reportadas para avaliação. Uma única ampliação foi estimada em mais de US$ 100 milhões. Esse valor parece descrever o valor de uma melhoria, e não uma cobrança tributária confirmada. Valor avaliado e imposto sobre propriedade são medidas diferentes. Os distritos tributários aplicam alíquotas aos valores avaliados depois de considerar isenções, classificações e outras regras. O registro público também não estabelece por quanto tempo a ampliação permaneceu fora do cadastro de avaliação. Esse cronograma influenciará se o condado pode ajustar avaliações anteriores e quanto de receita adicional poderá resultar disso. Os avaliadores de Washington avaliam imóveis, incluindo edifícios qualificados e melhorias permanentes. As empresas também declaram bens pessoais tributáveis mantidos em 1º de janeiro. Em um data center, essa distinção pode separar um edifício de servidores, sistemas elétricos e outros ativos móveis. O calendário publicado pelo Condado de Grant informa que os proprietários devem apresentar seus relatórios de bens pessoais ao avaliador. Enquanto isso, licenças de construção e inspeções físicas ajudam o condado a identificar mudanças em imóveis. Um campus hyperscale complica ambos os processos. Sua estrutura visível representa apenas uma parte do investimento. Distribuição de energia, sistemas de resfriamento, geradores, subestações, equipamentos de rede e instalações de servidores podem chegar por meio de projetos separados. A propriedade também pode ser dividida entre um proprietário de terreno, operador da instalação, empresa de nuvem e inquilino. Uma licença pode identificar uma parte, enquanto o equipamento tributável pertence a outra. Isso cria vários possíveis pontos de falha. Uma estrutura concluída pode não chegar prontamente ao avaliador. Uma declaração do proprietário pode omitir uma instalação. Os registros também podem classificar uma melhoria de forma diferente do tratamento final dado pelo avaliador. As evidências atuais não identificam qual explicação se aplica a cada discrepância no Condado de Grant. Seria prematuro descrever o caso como evasão intencional sem registros que o sustentem ou uma constatação oficial. No entanto, a escala elimina qualquer possibilidade de que se tratasse de uma questão trivial de documentação. Uma melhoria avaliada em mais de US$ 100 milhões pode alterar materialmente a avaliação de uma parcela e a distribuição das obrigações tributárias locais. A próxima etapa é a conciliação. A equipe do condado precisará comparar licenças, registros de inspeção, declarações de propriedade, datas de conclusão e fichas de avaliação anteriores. Os operadores devem ter a oportunidade de fornecer documentação e contestar qualquer valor proposto. Esse processo pode produzir uma avaliação mais alta sem gerar um aumento idêntico na receita do governo local. O sistema de alíquotas de Washington inclui limites de taxa e cálculos específicos por distrito que podem redistribuir as cargas tributárias entre proprietários. Ainda assim, incluir o valor omitido no cadastro é importante. Isso garante que grandes propriedades industriais recebam o mesmo escrutínio esperado de residências, fazendas, lojas e outras empresas. Por Que Uma Ampliação de Nove Dígitos Pode Ficar Fora do Cadastro Tributário Os data centers de IA expõem os limites de sistemas de avaliação projetados para ciclos de construção mais lentos e visíveis. Um projeto industrial convencional geralmente segue uma sequência reconhecível. O proprietário apresenta planos, obtém licenças, conclui inspeções e inaugura um edifício finalizado. Essa sequência cria várias oportunidades para que o avaliador identifique novo valor tributável. Os campi modernos de data centers nem sempre se desenvolvem de maneira tão organizada. Os operadores adicionam salas, sistemas de resfriamento, pátios elétricos, geradores e capacidade de servidores em fases sobrepostas. artigo.texto: Battery banks are (rightfully) getting a bit of a reputation on planes these days, so safer, more stable options are needed. Enter the LASER ChargeCore Powerbank range using new semi-solid state battery tech, offering enhanced battery safety and stability. LASER has been at the forefront of powerbanks, even introducing the newer LiFePO4 batteries to their battery banks last year, and are now introducing semi-solid state batteries with a focus on safety and peace of mind. Chris Lau, Managing Director of LASER said “We’ve been closely following semi solid state battery development for some time, since first visiting an EV factory several years ago, and advancements since that time mean that it can now move into smaller, more compact options. Simply put, I believe that Semi Solid State chemistry makes this the safest powerbank technology available in Australia today. We are focused on safety and peace of mind, and we know that it is a huge concern for Australian consumers these days when buying powerbanks.” The new ChargeCore PowerBanks come in three capacities, 10,000mAh, 20,000mAh and 27,000mAh offering a USB Type-C and two USB-A ports giving you versatile charging for your phones, tablets and more. The 10k and 20kmAh PowerBanks are able to deliver 20W of power across the three ports, while the 27,000mAh option can charge devices at up to 35W. All three models include an easy-to-read digital battery display showing how much is left, as well as including integrated protection against overcharging, overcurrent, short circuits and overheating. The new ChargeCore PowerBanks are available now in Black, with LASER also announcing Galactica, Grey, and Dark Cherry colour options are coming soon for their 10K and 20K ChargeCore PowerBanks. While the ChargeCore range is arriving now, LASER is also looking ahead, with Magnetic Charging and Waterproof options also using the semi-solid state battery tech coming soon. You can find the new ChargeCore Everyday Semi Solid State Series at Harvey Norman and Laser Online. The 10,000mAh with 20W USB-C PDis priced at .95, while the 20,000mAh with 20W USB-C PD is priced at .95. Lastly, the 27,000mAh ChargeCore PowerBank with 35W USB-C PD charging is priced at .95. artigo.texto: President Donald Trump said that data center companies should pay local communities a "dividend" to make their projects "popular." In a Truth Social post early Wednesday, Trump urged companies to "MAKE DEALS," but did not provide details on how much money they should return to communities or individuals where data centers are being built. "I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," he wrote in the post. There's been a growing backlash against data center construction across the US, with some saying the projects are noisy, raise electricity bills, and compromise the general quality of living. Data centers are becoming an increasingly important issue in next month's midterm elections, and some politicians have shifted how they talk about the projects in recent months. Data Center Watch, a research project run by 10a Labs, found that in the first quarter of this year, at least 75 data center projects were delayed or canceled due to local opposition. Some companies have already started trying to placate unhappy locals with money or discounts. This summer, Elon Musk's SpaceX offered eligible Memphis residents a 50% discount on its Starlink internet service, tied to its growing AI build-out in the city. NorthPoint Development opted for a pure cash incentive and said it would pay every household in a Pennsylvania township $10,000 if it got permission to build a data center, the Wall Street Journal reported last month. In his Wednesday post, Trump also referenced one of his previous efforts: having tech companies cover their power costs when they build data centers to help keep local electricity prices flat. Several tech leaders agreed to do so in March, when they signed the "Ratepayer Protection Pledge," which mandates that companies provide or pay for the power generation and electricity needed for their AI projects, among other commitments. Trump closed his Wednesday post by saying that building data centers under his newest stipulations would be "GREAT FOR THE U.S.A."

artigo.texto: Promovido pelo fundo Aura Capital, através da Aura Technologies, que se apresenta como uma plataforma europeia de investimento e desenvolvimento focada em infraestrutura digital, o projeto prevê a instalação, no Parque Empresarial do Sorraia, do primeiro de uma rede de centros de dados “compactos” para treino e inferência de inteligência artificial (IA). A rede deverá estender-se a Espanha e ao sul de França, avançou o ECO. Com 6,4 MW, a capacidade ficará quase ao nível da do centro de dados da Covilhã. O objetivo é que a nova infraestrutura entre em funcionamento no final de 2027, empregando cerca de 30 pessoas. Segundo a informação publicada pelo SAPO, a empresa veículo para este projeto é a Nextgen AIDC Coruche, com sede na incubadora de empresas de Coruche, que pediu à Câmara Municipal que retirasse os ónus e encargos associados a um terreno no Parque Empresarial do Sorraia, avaliado em cerca de 180.000 mil euros. A proposta já foi aprovada em reunião do executivo, com os votos favoráveis dos três eleitos do PS e a abstenção dos quatro vereadores da oposição, do Movimento Volta Coruche e do PSD. O anúncio surge numa altura em que a associação ambientalista Quercus contabiliza 46 centros de dados já existentes em Portugal, 25 em Lisboa e 11 no Porto. O Governo admite poder vir a somar mais 44, quatro deles de grande dimensão, o que elevaria para 90 o número de infraestruturas deste tipo em território nacional.

artigo.texto: Professor David S. Levine discusses trade secret protections, nondisclosure agreements and proposed federal legislation to improve public access to information around data centers. As Congress considers legislation to increase transparency in data center development, Elon University School of Law Professor David S. Levine recently discussed how trade secret protections and nondisclosure agreements can prevent the public from learning how taxpayer resources are used and how projects affect local communities. An Oct. 14 article published by MLex, “Trade secrets could constrain US legislative push to open data center deals,” examines the bipartisan No Secrets for Data Centers Act BILL, which would restrict non-disclosure agreements between data center developers and public officials. MLex, a LexisNexis news service, covers legal and regulatory developments for attorneys, businesses and government agencies. “The public expects transparency and accountability when it comes to allocation of taxpayer funds … NDAs piled on top of robust trade secret protection leaves the public largely blind. Given this compounded secrecy, the likelihood of corruption increases,” Levine told MLex. Levine, who studies trade secrecy and information law, also discusses how existing trade secret protections could continue to limit public access to information even if non-disclosure agreements were prohibited, preventing access to information about environmental, health, and safety risks and where public money is going. an area of focus, Levine was consulted by then-vice president Joe Biden’s staff regarding NDAs and trade secrecy during the second Obama administration. Read the full article at MLex. A subscription is required.

artigo.texto: Ten Reputable Solar Energy Storage Battery Manufacturers in China 2026: Advancing Clean Energy Storage Press Release Date 10-20-2026 A 2026 guide to ten reputable Chinese manufacturers of solar energy storage batteries. CALIFORNIA, CA, UNITED STATES, October 20, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- SHENZHEN, China, October 21, 2026 — Shenzhen Topway New Energy Co., Ltd., a lithium battery pack manufacturer based in Bao'an District, Shenzhen and trading as HCC, heads a ten-company editorial list of Chinese solar energy storage battery manufacturers published today. The list places the company alongside nine further Chinese battery producers whose storage products are sold in domestic and export markets. The review assesses companies on four criteria that are observable from public information: breadth of in-house research and engineering, certification coverage relevant to export markets, manufacturing footprint, and the range of storage applications served. It is an editorial assessment compiled from company information and third-party market data. It is not a third-party ranking, and no company paid for inclusion. The list is published as demand for battery energy storage systems expands. Grand View Research estimated the global Battery Energy Storage System market at approximately USD 13.2 billion in 2025, with a projected value of USD 99.7 billion by 2033, and reported that lithium-ion batteries accounted for 53.5% of the segment in 2025. Industry context: demand growth and tightening standards Storage demand is being shaped by two forces at once. The first is volume: utility, commercial and residential installations all require cell and pack supply, and the same cell chemistries now compete across all three. The second is standardisation, which changes what qualifies as a credible supplier. Three documents anchor the compliance side of the market. IEC 62619:2022 is the current international safety standard for lithium-ion batteries in industrial and stationary applications, and covers thermal runaway behaviour and battery management system verification. UL 1973 is the primary North American safety standard for batteries in stationary applications such as solar energy storage and uninterruptible power supplies. UN 38.3 governs the transport of lithium batteries globally and requires eight specific tests, including altitude simulation and thermal testing. Segment demand is uneven. Mordor Intelligence and Strategic Market Research estimated the global golf cart battery market at USD 1.49 billion in 2024, with lithium-ion types capturing a 47.18% share — a reminder that storage chemistries are displacing lead-acid in motive applications at the same time as they scale in stationary ones. How the ten companies were assessed The four criteria were applied consistently across all ten companies, and each company is described only on the basis of publicly stated business scope. The criteria are: Technical research and engineering. Whether a company operates its own development capability for cells, modules or packs, and whether that capability extends to custom configurations rather than catalogue-only products. Certification coverage. Whether products are documented against RoHS, CE, UL or equivalent schemes, since these determine access to European and North American channels. Manufacturing footprint. Plant area, headcount and production arrangements, used as an indicator of how much of the value chain a supplier controls directly. Application and solution breadth. The range of use cases served, from residential wall-mounted systems to golf cart traction packs, industrial backup and commercial peak-shaving configurations. No single criterion decides placement. Companies with large cell output but limited pack-level customisation are not treated as equivalent to companies that design and assemble complete packs for specific applications. The ten manufacturers 1. Shenzhen Topway New Energy Co., Ltd. (HCC) Founded in 2022, Shenzhen Topway New Energy operates from a 10,000 m² facility in Bao'an District, Shenzhen, with 200 employees and a 15-person R&D team, and states an export ratio of 40% across markets including the United States, Germany, Italy, Poland, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam and Australia. Its storage range covers the Wall-TW01 5 kW wall-mounted battery, built on LiFePO4 cells rated for at least 6,000 cycles at 80% capacity with a maximum continuous discharge current of 50 A; a 48 V 280 Ah solar battery pack rated at 200 A continuous discharge; a 51.2 V 200 Ah unit; 51.2 V 100 Ah and 48 V 100 Ah models; and 25.6 V 100 Ah and 12.8 V 100 Ah units. A 51.2 V 105 Ah pack serves golf cart traction. Products carry RoHS, UL and CE certification. The company states that it is moving from pack solutions and cooperative production toward in-house manufacturing with new production lines, and it also lists robot, exoskeleton and drone battery packs among its product lines — a breadth that supports custom pack engineering rather than single-format assembly. 2. Its position on the list reflects the depth of its cell engineering and its role as a cell supplier to system integrators, which places its products inside a large share of finished storage installations rather than only in direct-sale configurations. 3. artigo.texto: A Microsoft (MSFT) desistiu de um planejado data center de IA em Loughton, Essex, que o provedor britânico de nuvem Nscale estava construindo para ela, informou a Reuters em 18 de outubro, citando o Telegraph. A Microsoft é um dos dois maiores clientes da Nscale. A Reuters disse que o Telegraph não especificou o motivo da retirada da Microsoft, e a Microsoft declinou comentar o pedido da Reuters. O local realmente tinha um problema óbvio: energia. O Telegraph informou que os oficiais da rede disseram à Nscale que não esperavam fornecer eletricidade até a década de 2030. Isso corresponde a um relatório de setembro de que a UK Power Networks não conseguiria conectar o local antes do início a meados da década de 2030. A Nscale diz que permanece comprometida com Loughton e está analisando outras fontes de energia. Loughton Era uma Pequena Fatia da Expansão da Microsoft Loughton foi planejado para abrigar cerca de 23.000 chips da Nvidia (NVDA) para o Azure, começando com 50 MW. A Nscale concordou em fornecer à Microsoft cerca de 200.000 chips da Nvidia no Reino Unido, Noruega, Portugal e Texas, então Loughton representava cerca de 11,5% do programa. A Microsoft adicionou aproximadamente um gigawatt de capacidade apenas no trimestre de junho, o que faz com que a carga inicial de Loughton seja cerca de 5% de um trimestre. Os gastos não mostram sinais de recuo. Os gastos de capital em caixa atingiram US$ 35,80 bilhões no trimestre de junho, mais que o dobro dos US$ 17,08 bilhões de um ano antes. O capex em caixa do ano fiscal de 2026 totalizou US$ 115,95 bilhões, um aumento de cerca de 80%. Na medida mais ampla da administração, incluindo arrendamentos financeiros, o capex do trimestre de junho foi de aproximadamente US$ 41 bilhões, com mais de US$ 50 bilhões esperados no trimestre de setembro. A demanda está acompanhando o ritmo. A receita da Nuvem Inteligente atingiu US$ 39,31 bilhões no trimestre de junho, um aumento de cerca de 32% em relação aos US$ 29,88 bilhões, e a CFO Amy Hood disse que a demanda dos clientes ainda excede a oferta disponível. artigo.texto: MHI partners with Ingeteam to advance power solutions for data centers The alliance combines MHI’s expertise in integrated power, cooling and energy management with Ingeteam’s expertise in rotating electrical machines, power electronics, control and automation and digital technologies. Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) and Spanish company Ingeteam have announced an MOU forming a strategic partnership to distribute, integrate and jointly develop advanced energy infrastructure solutions for US data Centers. The alliance combines MHI’s expertise in integrated power, cooling and energy management with Ingeteam’s expertise in rotating electrical machines, power electronics, control and automation and digital technologies, helping data center operators address power quality and grid-integration challenges created by next-generation AI workloads, according to a press release. MHI Group brings a systems integration approach to AI data center infrastructure with decades of experience delivering large-scale energy systems, industrial cooling systems and complex infrastructure projects. Ingeteam brings more than five decades of industrial and technological experience, combining engineering and manufacturing capabilities in power conversion systems for power generation, grid integration, control and automation, and energy management. Its technology portfolio encompasses electrical generators, advanced power electronics architectures, battery energy storage solutions, power quality and grid stability technologies, and EMS/SCADA control platforms, the press release said. Through this alliance, MHI and Ingeteam intend to collaborate on expanding the availability of Ingeteam's power conversion solutions and related software for the U.S. data center market through MHI Group, while exploring opportunities to integrate selected technologies into advanced energy infrastructure architectures and solutions developed by MHI Group for its customers. “Ingeteam's depth in power electronics and power conversion strengthens our ability to deliver complete, reliable solutions for our U.S. data center customers developing AI Data Centers,” said Shin Gomi, Senior General Manager, Data Center & Energy Management Department at MHI. “This alliance lets Ingeteam bring our power electronics and grid expertise to U.S. data centers alongside a partner with deep systems-engineering capability,” said Adolfo Rebollo, Chief Executive Officer, Ingeteam. “Together, we can provide a bridge between the electric grid and next-generation AI infrastructure, enabling customers to scale computing capacity while maintaining reliability and efficiency.”

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition. BYD Brings Flash Charging to Indonesia with New DENZA Models BYD introduced its second-generation Blade Battery and Flash Charging technology in Indonesia, marking the technology's overseas debut. The announcement coincided with the launch of two new DENZA models, the D9 and the Z9GT, as BYD expands its electric vehicle lineup and charging services in the Southeast Asian market. According to BYD, its Flash Charging technology can charge a battery from 10% to 70% in as little as five minutes, and from 10% to 97% in nine minutes under normal conditions. The system integrates energy storage with charging equipment and features a lightweight charging connector designed to make plugging in easier, as well as a plug-and-charge function. To support the rollout, BYD plans to install Flash Charging equipment at 10 DENZA dealerships in Indonesia in the initial phase. The stations will be open to the public, providing an initial charging network before the company expands coverage further. The new DENZA D9 comes equipped with the second-generation Blade Battery and Flash Charging technology, alongside upgrades to powertrain performance, driving range and comfort. The Z9GT, meanwhile, is built on BYD's e³ platform, extending the brand's premium electric vehicle offering in Indonesia. Huawei-Backed Yinwang Teams Up with CATL on Automated Battery Swapping Yinwang Intelligent Technology, a Huawei-affiliated smart vehicle company, has signed a strategic cooperation agreement with CATL and its battery-swapping subsidiary, Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology, to develop an intelligent battery-swapping ecosystem for autonomous vehicles. The agreement was signed on October 19 and covers vehicle integration, swappable batteries and network development. The three companies plan to connect vehicles, battery-swapping stations and cloud systems, using real-time battery data and drivers' travel patterns to predict energy needs and coordinate services. The proposed system would allow vehicles to determine when a battery swap is needed, locate a station, enter and align automatically, complete the swap in just 99 seconds, and drive away without human intervention. The partnership brings Yinwang into CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem. The companies will adapt participating vehicle models to work with the network, with the aim of expanding access to battery-swapping services for vehicles equipped with Huawei's Qiankun intelligent automotive solutions. CATL's Choco-Swap network had 2,520 stations across 200 Chinese cities as of September 29. The company plans to expand the network to 30,000 stations and connect urban and highway coverage, although the announcement did not specify a timeline for reaching that target. The deal highlights how Chinese companies are working to integrate automated driving with energy replenishment. By linking vehicle intelligence, cloud-based service coordination and battery-swapping infrastructure, the partners aim to make battery replacement faster and more convenient while extending the service network available to intelligent vehicles. Schaeffler Opens Humanoid Robot Factory in China Schaeffler opened a humanoid robotics factory in Taicang, Jiangsu province, on October 20, bringing robot-component manufacturing, robot training and industrial applications together under one roof. Spanning approximately 7,500 square meters, the facility is designed to help move humanoid robots from experimental projects into real-world manufacturing. Six humanoid robots are already working on an assembly line producing joint modules for other humanoid robots. Across five workstations, they handle tasks including material handling, parts sorting, press-fitting, inspection and packaging. The setup marks a step toward a closed manufacturing loop in which humanoid robots help produce components for the next generation of robots. The factory also includes dedicated training environments for industrial tasks such as visual inspection, material picking and component assembly. A digital-twin system connects robot training with production validation and process optimization, allowing Schaeffler to test and refine processes virtually before implementing changes on the actual production line. The opening comes as Schaeffler expands its humanoid robotics business in China. The company said it secured orders from two new Chinese customers in the third quarter of 2026, bringing its cumulative global order intake in humanoid robotics to approximately €400 million. The Taicang facility will also serve as a platform for collaboration with Chinese robotics companies.

artigo.texto: Yasin Gungor 21 October 2026•Update: 21 October 2026 US President Donald Trump on Wednesday urged operators of large artificial intelligence data centers to strike financial agreements with local communities and pay them dividends to ease public backlash over rising energy costs. "If companies want to make their data centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a 'dividend,'" Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social, arguing that projects facing fierce local opposition quickly gain acceptance once direct economic pacts are reached. Trump said facilities must produce their own power rather than draining public utilities. He maintained that new and large data centers are required to "make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid," asserting that such measures would prevent utility inflation and potentially yield "a substantial decrease" in electricity rates. The US has more than 5,000 data centers, with facilities projected to expand roughly 9% annually through 2030, according to the US Department of Commerce. The directive comes amid escalating friction over power consumption driven by the artificial intelligence boom ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Public surveys show strong bipartisan opposition, with a Gallup poll finding 71% of Americans resisting local developments over concerns that facilities will inflate residential utility bills. The policy builds upon Trump's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge established in March, which called on technology firms to cover all power generation and transmission costs.

artigo.texto: GREEN CHARTER TOWNSHIP, Mich. (Michigan News Source) – After years of controversy, lawsuits and political battles, the proposed Gotion electric vehicle battery plant in Mecosta County is heading toward a legal conclusion. And the current price tag for settling one federal claim? One dollar. Township Approves Settlement The Green Charter Township Board of Trustees approved a proposed settlement agreement on Thursday, October 15 during a special meeting, potentially ending litigation involving Gotion Inc. and its controversial battery plant project. MORE NEWS: Trump Calls Slotkin a ‘Lowlife’ Over Remarks About Young Trump Administration Recruits According to the Big Rapids Pioneer, the agreement requires Gotion to transfer the proposed project property to the Michigan State Land Bank. The Michigan Strategic Fund would also drop its demand against Gotion involving grant funds. The township would refund certain project-related funds and remove some public statements concerning Gotion, the litigation, and economic development organization The Right Place. One Dollar and Done? Under the agreement, Gotion would receive a consent judgment on one federal claim with just $1 in damages. All remaining claims would be dismissed with prejudice, preventing them from being refiled. The parties would also terminate project agreements and release claims against one another related to the dispute. Township attorney Kyle O’Meara said the agreement follows negotiations culminating in an October 2 settlement conference before a federal magistrate judge. Although the township has approved the terms, final paperwork may still require additional board approval. MORE NEWS: Political Signs Spark Owosso Farmers Market Showdown; GOP Alleges Double Standard For residents who fought the controversial project, the proposed settlement signals that the long-running battle over the battery plant is finally moving toward a conclusion. Cella: Gotion Deal Was a Threat to National Security Joseph Cella, director and co-founder of the Michigan China Economic Security and Review Group, who has been a vocal opponent of the Gotion battery plant project, called the agreement between government officials and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)-linked company corrupt from the beginning. He said in a statement to Michigan News Source, “It moved fast and in secret and it ruptured the consent of the governed,” He accused officials of failing to conduct proper due diligence and ignoring national security concerns, describing the project as having “all of the textbook markings of a subnational incursion and influence operation by a CCP-tied entity.” Cella credited local residents for defeating the project, saying it would not have happened without the patriots of Mecosta County who “courageously stood up, exposed it, tenaciously fought it, and ultimately restored the consent of the governed.”

artigo.texto: Africa’s ambition to turn carbon credits into a major source of climate finance faces a fundamental obstacle: investors want projects that are ready for financing, but developers often lack the money needed to prepare them. Teddy Mugabo, Chief Executive Officer of the Rwanda Green Fund, raised the concern during the Carbon Markets Africa Summit in Kigali, where she joined a panel discussion titled “What Are Investors Actually Funding and Why?” “If we want more investable African carbon projects, someone must invest in making them investable,” Mugabo said. Her argument highlights a financing gap affecting African climate projects. Before a project can attract commercial investment, developers must often finance feasibility studies, establish emissions baselines, prepare technical documentation and demonstrate that the expected carbon reductions can be independently verified. These preliminary activities require capital, yet investors frequently prefer to commit funding only after such requirements have been met. Mugabo called for patient capital and shared financial risks involving governments, development partners, project developers and private investors. The challenge is particularly significant given Africa’s ambitions in the global carbon market. The Africa Carbon Markets Initiative has outlined an ambition to generate 300 million carbon credits annually by 2030, potentially unlocking $6 billion in revenue and supporting 30 million jobs. These figures represent targets and projections, not realised market outcomes. The summit, held at the Kigali Convention Centre from October 13 to 15, brought together more than 500 participants, including investors, project developers, government representatives and carbon credit buyers. Organisers showcased more than 40 projects and programmes, including at least 8 opportunities presented as investment-ready. Rwanda has already established a National Carbon Market Framework under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, providing procedures for developing, approving and trading carbon credits. In March 2025, Rwanda also launched an $854,859 programme with the Global Green Growth Institute to strengthen its readiness for international carbon markets. The country has experience in carbon credit generation. Government figures show that more than 2.25 million credits had been issued by December 2020, with improved cookstove projects accounting for 87% of certified emission reductions reported in its historical portfolio. However, expanding the market beyond established activities into larger forestry, agriculture, energy and industrial projects requires credible project pipelines and financing mechanisms that can absorb early-stage risks. For Mugabo, the immediate priority is therefore not simply attracting more investors, but ensuring that promising African projects receive the preparation funding needed to meet investment standards. Without that support, Africa risks having substantial carbon market potential on paper while too few projects reach the stage where investors are willing to finance them.

artigo.texto: Área técnica da Aneel quer repasse de transmissoras no leilão de baterias Ofício conjunto vincula participação das empresas à destinação de parte ou total da receita dos projetos à redução das tarifas de transmissão A área técnica da Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) defende que a participação de transmissoras nos leilões de baterias depende da reversão de parte da receita da atividade para reduzir as tarifas. O entendimento consta de Ofício Conjunto obtido pela reportagem que também exige autorização prévia da agência para participação nos certames e separação contábil, financeira e contratual entre os negócios. A orientação se apoia em um parecer da Procuradoria Federal junto à Aneel. O documento corrobora o entendimento da procuradoria de que estaria sendo prestado um serviço de engenharia pelas Transmissoras. O ofício responde a uma consulta apresentada pela Taesa sobre a participação de concessionárias de transmissão no leilão de baterias, previsto para ocorrer em dezembro. A Taesa apresentou contribuições na Consulta Pública instaurada pela Aneel sobre o leilão afirmando que condicionar a participação de transmissoras nos eventos à reversão de receitas para reduzir as tarifas de transmissão torna a entrada desses agentes economicamente inviável e impõe uma retenção ilegítima de receita autorizada em outra modalidade de atuação (armazenador). A companhia sustenta que a exigência cria uma desvantagem na disputa e pode encarecer a contratação de armazenamento, custeada pelos geradores de energia. O ofício, contudo, diz que a obrigação de beneficiar as tarifas de transmissão permanece quando o armazenamento é explorado por uma SPE (Sociedade de Propósito Específico) da transmissão, ainda que juridicamente independente da concessionária. “Além disso, mantém-se a necessidade do benefício à modicidade tarifária, mediante reversão total ou parcial das receitas auferidas com a atividade da SPE para a concessão, em favor dos usuários do SIN [Sistema Interligado Nacional]”. Ainda segundo o ofício, os contratos firmados exigem autorização prévia para atividades estranhas ao objeto da concessão e estabelecem que parte ou toda a receita desses negócios contribua para a modicidade das tarifas de transmissão. O ofício não define percentual, base de cálculo ou metodologia para a reversão. O texto usa a expressão “receitas auferidas com a atividade da SPE”, sem individualizar a receita fixa do CRCap (Contrato de Reserva de Capacidade para Potência). Vale destacar que a manifestação é das áreas técnicas; o documento não registra uma deliberação da diretoria colegiada da agência sobre os editais ou sobre a legitimidade dessa captura. A Aneel já autorizou a ISA Energia Brasil a oferecer serviços de eficiência energética com baterias diretamente a empresas, com compartilhamento de receitas para reduzir as tarifas de transmissão, segundo ao portal MegaWhat. Nesse caso, os serviços são contratados por clientes privados. Nos leilões, o pagamento será pela disponibilidade de potência para atender o sistema elétrico, com custos divididos entre os geradores. Transmissoras podem ficar de fora Fontes ouvidas pela reportagem dizem que se o entendimento for mantido, as empresas transmissoras podem ficar de fora do leilão por perda de concorrência e desequilíbrio dos investimentos. Nas contribuições à Consulta Pública do leilão, a Taesa afirma que a autorização adicional e a reversão de receitas não constam das minutas dos editais nem das notas técnicas que embasam os certames. Na avaliação da companhia, o tema precisa ser definido de forma geral, isonômica e transparente antes da aprovação dos editais, porque todos os empreendedores interessados no certame devem competir em igualdade. “A Receita Fixa do CRCap não se sujeita a reversão à modicidade tarifária da transmissão”, sustenta a Taesa em um dos tópicos da contribuição. Como os certames selecionam propostas de menor receita fixa, uma subsidiária de transmissora sujeita à reversão precisaria incorporar esse custo ao lance ou aceitar remuneração líquida inferior à de concorrentes com as mesmas obrigações contratuais. A reportagem procurou a Abrate, associação que representa as empresas transmissoras. Em nota a entidade disse que apresentou contribuições às Consultas Públicas nº 22 e 23/2026, relativas aos Leilões de Reserva de Capacidade para Sistemas de Armazenamento de Energia (SAE), com foco em apenas três aspectos: Área de Desenvolvimento da Subestação (ADS); Riscos de Escoamento e Conexão à Rede; e Inadimplência Intrasetorial. No que diz respeito à referida regra de captura de receitas de SPEs de armazenamento controladas por transmissoras no leilão de baterias, “a Abrate informa que, até o momento, esta não é uma agenda setorial da entidade, tratando-se de uma demanda específica de algumas associadas, e portanto, não emite manifestações sobre o tema, mas segue acompanhando”, diz o comunicado.

artigo.texto: Expansão de Data Centers no Brasil Vai Além de São Paulo, mas a Rede Elétrica Decide o Que Será Construído A expansão dos data centers no Brasil foi além de São Paulo, embora esse mercado ainda concentre 76% da capacidade operacional do país. Desenvolvedores agora buscam projetos em escala de gigawatts no Rio de Janeiro, Ceará e Rio Grande do Sul. A mudança promete mais capacidade regional, mas também expõe uma restrição difícil. Energia anunciada não é o mesmo que energia conectada. A história imediata não é a perda do status de São Paulo como capital computacional do Brasil. Seus clientes, densidade de rede, infraestrutura de nuvem e operadores estabelecidos continuam difíceis de igualar. A mudança é que a infraestrutura de IA exige mais eletricidade e terreno do que o cluster tradicional pode fornecer com facilidade. Rio AI City, o mercado de Fortaleza conectado por cabos e a Scala AI City no Sul do Brasil oferecem alternativas diferentes. Juntos, eles desafiam a suposição de que quase toda grande implantação precisa permanecer próxima de São Paulo. Ainda assim, suas enormes metas de capacidade descrevem sobretudo futuros campi, não servidores que já processam cargas de trabalho. Essa distinção define a próxima fase do crescimento dos data centers no Brasil. Incentivos fiscais podem reduzir custos de equipamentos, enquanto a energia renovável pode fortalecer a tese de investimento. Nenhuma dessas vantagens elimina a construção de linhas de transmissão, análises ambientais ou a necessidade de fibra confiável e clientes. A Expansão dos Data Centers no Brasil Está se Tornando uma História Nacional O mercado deixou de ser uma exploração regional e passou a uma disputa entre diversos polos de infraestrutura distintos. São Paulo continua sendo o centro de gravidade. Segundo a análise de mercado original, o mercado metropolitano responde por 76% da capacidade operacional de data centers do Brasil. Ele combina a maior base de clientes do país com fibra densa, pontos de acesso à nuvem e campi de colocation consolidados. Essas vantagens se reforçam mutuamente. Empresas colocam cargas de trabalho perto de regiões de nuvem e pontos de troca de tráfego. Em seguida, operadores expandem onde já há demanda e opções de interconexão. Novos clientes recebem uma escolha maior de provedores, o que atrai ainda mais infraestrutura. Esse ciclo explica por que os data centers de São Paulo dominaram por tanto tempo. Também explica por que os mercados regionais não substituirão a cidade simplesmente oferecendo terrenos mais baratos. Um novo local precisa fornecer eletricidade, telecomunicações resilientes, trabalhadores qualificados e um caminho convincente para a demanda dos clientes. No entanto, as exigências da computação de IA estão mudando a seleção de locais. Clusters de alta densidade podem exigir compromissos de energia muito maiores do que implantações empresariais convencionais. Por isso, os desenvolvedores precisam de locais onde terreno e eletricidade possam sustentar campi em fases, medidos em centenas de megawatts. O Rio de Janeiro está se apresentando como um polo de IA e nuvem, e não como uma cópia menor de São Paulo. A Rio AI City combina uma instalação existente da Elea com um campus proposto ao redor do Parque Olímpico. O plano prevê 1,5 gigawatt inicialmente e 3 gigawatts até 2032. Um anúncio de junho de 2026 vinculou esse plano a um investimento de US$ 550 milhões na plataforma mais ampla de infraestrutura da Elea. Autoridades municipais disseram que o financiamento poderia iniciar um ciclo mais longo de expansão, chegando a US$ 10 bilhões. Esses números abrangem ambições e capacidade de financiamento, não salas de data center concluídas. Fortaleza oferece uma proposta diferente. A cidade está próxima de um grupo incomumente denso de pontos de aterragem de cabos submarinos que conectam o Brasil à América do Norte, Europa, África e outros mercados latino-americanos. Essa posição pode reduzir a dependência de rotas que passam pelo Sudeste brasileiro. A conectividade internacional dá a Fortaleza um papel crível em serviços de nuvem, distribuição de conteúdo e processamento de dados para exportação. Também torna o Ceará relevante para operadores que buscam energia renovável perto de uma grande porta de entrada de cabos. Essa combinação atraiu novos campi e expansões de instalações existentes. No Rio Grande do Sul, o argumento se concentra em terrenos disponíveis, energia renovável e acesso ao Cone Sul. O estado faz fronteira com Argentina e Uruguai, enquanto o Paraguai pode ser alcançado por redes regionais. Porto Alegre já sustenta um mercado menor de colocation que pode ancorar um desenvolvimento mais amplo. A Scala AI City ilustra a escala dessa ambição. O projeto em Eldorado do Sul começa com 54 megawatts planejados de capacidade de TI e tem potencial declarado de expansão para 4,75 gigawatts. A meta total abrange um horizonte de desenvolvimento longo, portanto não deve ser confundida com oferta operacional. Cada região busca um papel diferente. O Rio quer um grande campus de IA próximo a uma importante economia urbana. Fortaleza combina energia com cabos internacionais. O Rio Grande do Sul oferece uma plataforma no Sul com espaço para desenvolvimento em múltiplas etapas. É por isso que a expansão dos data centers no Brasil está se tornando uma história de infraestrutura nacional. Os locais emergentes não são intercambiáveis e não competem apenas por terreno. Cada um precisa transformar uma vantagem regional em capacidade computacional confiável. A Liderança de São Paulo É Tanto uma Vantagem Quanto uma Restrição A infraestrutura madura de São Paulo mantém sua predominância, mas essa mesma concentração agora dificulta a expansão. O ecossistema existente da cidade oferece uma certeza que os mercados emergentes não conseguem reproduzir imediatamente. Clientes podem escolher entre operadores estabelecidos, conectar-se a diversas redes e acessar grandes plataformas de nuvem. Desenvolvedores tamb
