artigo.texto: Resumo - Nscale negocia vender capacidade à Anthropic em acordo de até US$ 45 bilhões - Seria o segundo grande contrato entre as duas empresas no complexo Monarch - Novo prédio teria 460 MW e usaria chips Vera Rubin, da Nvidia - Acordos já firmados entre as empresas somam até US$ 44,6 bilhões A Anthropic, responsável pelo chatbot Claude, negocia com a Nscale um contrato de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA) que pode alcançar US$ 45 bilhões. A informação é de pessoas próximas às negociações. A Nscale, empresa de computação em nuvem apoiada pela Nvidia, pretende fechar um novo acordo para ampliar sua operação nos Estados Unidos. Dessa vez, o contrato envolve uma segunda instalação no complexo de data centers Monarch, na Virgínia Ocidental. As duas companhias já mantêm contratos de infraestrutura que somam aproximadamente US$ 44,6 bilhões. Os valores aparecem em documentos regulatórios relacionados à oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO) da Nscale. Novo prédio terá chips Vera Rubin da Nvidia O novo edifício do complexo Monarch poderá oferecer 460 megawatts de capacidade computacional. Para sustentar a operação, a Nscale pretende utilizar chips de inteligência artificial Vera Rubin, desenvolvidos pela Nvidia. Além disso, a Anthropic poderá obter preferência na contratação de um terceiro prédio que a Nscale planeja construir no mesmo campus. Segundo fontes ouvidas sob anonimato, as empresas podem concluir o acordo nos próximos dias. No entanto, as negociações continuam e ainda podem sofrer alterações. Procuradas, Anthropic e Nscale não comentaram o assunto. Quando estiver totalmente concluído, o complexo Monarch poderá ultrapassar 8 gigawatts de capacidade elétrica bruta, conforme os documentos do IPO. Inicialmente, a Microsoft ocuparia parte das instalações. Em março, a companhia chegou a anunciar uma carta de intenções para participar do projeto. Entretanto, segundo a Bloomberg News, a Microsoft desistiu da instalação durante o verão do hemisfério norte. Com a decisão, a Anthropic ganhou espaço para ampliar sua presença no complexo. IPO da Nscale e a corrida por data centers O possível contrato de US$ 45 bilhões surge em um momento estratégico para a Nscale. A companhia prepara sua estreia na Bolsa e busca alcançar uma avaliação de mercado próxima de US$ 30 bilhões. Nesse cenário, um novo acordo bilionário poderia fortalecer o interesse dos investidores na oferta. Apesar disso, parte do mercado pressiona a empresa a reduzir sua expectativa de valuation, segundo informações anteriores da Bloomberg. Enquanto isso, a Anthropic amplia seus investimentos em infraestrutura para acompanhar o crescimento da demanda por inteligência artificial. A companhia já firmou outros contratos bilionários para garantir capacidade computacional. Entre eles, estão acordos de US$ 50 bilhões com a Fluidstack e US$ 10 bilhões com a startup Volta. Além disso, a empresa fechou um compromisso de US$ 45 bilhões com a SpaceX, de Elon Musk. Com esses investimentos, a Anthropic se tornou uma das principais responsáveis pelo avanço da demanda global por data centers voltados à IA. Em maio, o mercado avaliava a companhia em aproximadamente US$ 965 bilhões. Agora, a empresa também aparece entre as possíveis candidatas a realizar um IPO nos próximos meses. Caso avance com a abertura de capital, a operação poderá figurar entre as maiores ofertas recentes do setor de tecnologia. Ao mesmo tempo, a expansão acelerada da infraestrutura de IA aumenta a preocupação dos investidores com o endividamento das empresas. Afinal, a construção de data centers exige investimentos elevados, muitas vezes financiados por meio de empréstimos e emissão de títulos de dívida. Essa preocupação já afetou diferentes segmentos do mercado, desde ações de fabricantes de chips até títulos emitidos por empresas de computação em nuvem. Apesar desse cenário, a Nscale mantém seus planos de abertura de capital nos Estados Unidos. A companhia apresentou o pedido de listagem em setembro, mas ainda não iniciou a divulgação formal da oferta. Atualmente, a empresa busca responder aos questionamentos da Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos Estados Unidos (SEC). Após concluir essa etapa, pretende iniciar o roadshow, período de apresentações aos potenciais investidores. Antes disso, em agosto, a Nscale levantou US$ 3,36 bilhões em uma rodada de investimentos pré-IPO. A operação teve a liderança da Third Point, gestora de Dan Loeb. A rodada também contou com aportes de Nvidia, Apollo Global Management, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital e Abu Dhabi Investment Council.

artigo.texto: Huawei’s automotive technology company Yinwang has signed a strategic agreement with CATL and its battery-swapping subsidiary Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology, or CAES. The companies will work on battery compatibility, swapping networks and the integration of Huawei’s Qiankun driving technology with CATL’s Choco-Swap system. The partnership will connect vehicle, station and cloud services, allowing vehicles to determine when they need a battery swap, find a station, enter and align themselves, complete a 99-second automated swap, and drive away. Yinwang will also work with its automotive partners to develop vehicles compatible with CATL’s swapping network. The agreement was signed in Ningde, Fujian province, on October 19. artigo.texto: Global clean energy brand BLUETTI showcased its portable power stations, residential energy storage systems, and commercial and industrial (C&I) energy solutions at the 140th Canton Fair, held from October 15 to 19, 2026. The exhibition highlighted the company’s products for personal, household, and business use while opening opportunities for partnerships with distributors and energy providers worldwide. The showcase covered solutions ranging from portable backup power to integrated solar, battery storage, and electric vehicle (EV) charging systems. BLUETTI also highlighted a pay-as-you-go financing model intended to make energy solutions more accessible to households and small businesses. Why it matters: Portable power and energy storage can help households and businesses manage power interruptions, while solar-powered systems offer another way to meet electricity needs. BLUETTI’s range of products also reflects the different requirements of individual users, residential customers, and commercial operations. The details: For portable power, BLUETTI presented its PREMIUM series, designed for outdoor activities, recreational vehicle travel, and home backup. It also showcased the Pioneer 5000, a professional portable power station rated for 5,000W of continuous output. The company said the Pioneer 5000 is designed for applications such as construction sites, equipment rental businesses, and agricultural operations. BLUETTI’s portable power solutions use lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery technology and support features such as fast charging, solar input, and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) protection. These features are intended to provide flexibility for users who need power in outdoor, residential, and professional settings. The bigger picture: BLUETTI also highlighted its HomeStar residential energy storage series, which supports AC and solar charging alongside app-based smart energy management. The company said these systems can serve households, clinics, and small businesses that need backup power. Another focus was BLUETTI’s integrated pay-as-you-go (PAYGO) solution, which uses flexible installment payments to make energy products more affordable. The BLUETTI GO platform supports digital operations management for the system. The company is inviting global partners to join its PAYGO solar network. Through platform integration, product deployment, and local distribution partnerships, BLUETTI aims to reach underserved households and micro-businesses, particularly in emerging markets. Between the lines: The PAYGO model is a key part of BLUETTI’s effort to expand beyond customers who can pay the full cost of an energy system upfront. Flexible payments may lower the initial financial barrier for eligible customers, while local distribution partners can help bring products to specific markets. However, the announcement does not provide detailed financing terms, eligibility requirements, or confirmed deployment plans for the Philippines. For businesses: BLUETTI’s commercial and industrial portfolio includes energy storage systems ranging from 64kWh to 240kWh, alongside integrated solar, storage, and EV charging solutions. The company said these systems can support peak shaving, energy arbitrage, backup power for critical loads, and flexible capacity expansion. By coordinating solar generation, battery storage, and EV charging demand, businesses may be able to manage peak electricity use, reduce reliance on the grid, and maintain operations during power disruptions. The potential benefits will depend on each installation’s energy demand, system configuration, local electricity rates, and operating conditions. What’s next: BLUETTI plans to strengthen its partnerships with distributors, energy developers, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractors, and other industry participants worldwide. The company aims to expand the deployment of its energy solutions across markets with different power requirements and business opportunities. BLUETTI reports serving more than 3.5 million customers worldwide and says it will continue developing products for personal, residential, and commercial applications. The Bottom Line: BLUETTI used the 140th Canton Fair to present its broader energy portfolio, from portable power stations and residential storage to large-scale commercial systems and PAYGO solar solutions. artigo.texto: O Brasil poderá ter o segundo menor custo do mundo para gerar energia solar firme em 2035, com cerca de US$ 41/MWh, segundo projeções da Agência Internacional de Energia Renovável (Irena). A estimativa considera a combinação de usinas solares fotovoltaicas com sistemas de armazenamento em baterias, capaz de fornecer eletricidade com 95% de confiabilidade. O país aparece empatado com Omã e atrás apenas da China, onde o custo projetado é de aproximadamente US$ 33/MWh. Os dados fazem parte do estudo 24/7 Renewables: The Economics of Firm Solar and Wind, da Irena, que analisa os custos de sistemas capazes de transformar a geração renovável variável em uma oferta de eletricidade mais previsível e disponível ao longo do dia. A redução dos preços dos módulos solares e dos sistemas de armazenamento está entre os principais fatores que impulsionam essa tendência. Na projeção para 2035, a China apresenta o menor custo de energia solar firme entre os mercados avaliados, com cerca de US$ 33/MWh. Brasil e Omã aparecem na sequência, com aproximadamente US$ 41/MWh, seguidos pela Índia, com US$ 47/MWh, e por Austrália e África do Sul, com cerca de US$ 50/MWh. Os Estados Unidos registram o maior custo projetado, próximo de US$ 59/MWh. A comparação considera locais com recursos renováveis de alta qualidade e um nível de confiabilidade de 95%. O custo nivelado de energia firme (LCOE, na sigla em inglês) estima quanto custa fornecer eletricidade com determinado nível de disponibilidade e confiabilidade, considerando as características do projeto, os recursos renováveis disponíveis e as condições de armazenamento. A métrica é calculada com base nas condições de cada projeto e localidade. Custo da energia solar firme pode cair até 2035 A Irena projeta que os custos da energia solar firme em mercados com condições favoráveis de geração, como Brasil, Índia, Omã, África do Sul e Austrália, reduzam para uma faixa de aproximadamente US$ 37/MWh a US$ 58/MWh até 2035. Em 2025, os custos estimados para esses mercados ficaram entre US$ 65/MWh e US$ 82/MWh. No Brasil, uma localidade de alta irradiação solar na Bahia apresentou custo de energia firme de aproximadamente US$ 65/MWh em 2025, com projeção de queda para cerca de US$ 44/MWh em 2030. O resultado coloca o local analisado entre as referências de competitividade para a combinação de geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento. A estimativa, porém, se aplica às condições específicas da localidade e não representa o custo médio da energia solar firme no Brasil. A redução dos custos das baterias é um dos principais fatores por trás desse movimento. Segundo a Irena, o custo global dos sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias caiu 93% entre 2010 e 2024, passando de US$ 2.634/kWh para US$ 197/kWh. A agência projeta que essa tendência continue até 2035. Entre os locais avaliados, os custos de energia solar firme devem variar de aproximadamente US$ 33/MWh, nas localidades de menor custo da China, a US$ 59/MWh nos Estados Unidos. Baterias podem ampliar a flexibilidade do sistema elétrico Para a Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar), a projeção reforça a competitividade do Brasil na combinação entre geração solar e armazenamento de energia. A entidade avalia que a redução dos custos das baterias e a evolução tecnológica podem ampliar a previsibilidade e a flexibilidade das fontes renováveis, permitindo atender a novos perfis de consumo e aproveitar melhor a infraestrutura elétrica existente. “Os resultados mostram que o Brasil reúne condições muito favoráveis para avançar na oferta de energia renovável firme e competitiva. A redução dos custos do armazenamento amplia a capacidade de utilizar o sol de forma mais estratégica, deslocando a geração para os momentos de maior necessidade do sistema”, afirma Rodrigo Sauaia, CEO da Absolar.

artigo.texto: Dow Launches VOLTRICELL Platform to Advance Battery Innovation Dow Inc. DOW recently launched VOLTRICELL, a new battery cell materials platform designed to optimize battery manufacturing and improve performance. The platform expands Dow’s battery solutions portfolio and strengthens its presence in the industry. Dow, which is among the leading companies in the chemical space, along with DuPont de Nemours, Inc. DD, Eastman Chemical Company EMN and Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. APD, aims to bring together materials for electrodes, separators, coatings and battery cell packaging, including binders, dispersants, rheology modifiers, surfactants and specialty additives, through VOLTRICELL. These materials are designed to support higher energy density, longer cycle life, faster charging and scalable manufacturing. The platform integrates emerging technologies such as sodium-ion, silicon-anode and solid-state batteries. The new launch will be complemented by VORAFORCE TP1415 polyurethane resin for lightweight, flame-retardant composites, DOWSIL EF-6559 silicone foam for thermal management and electrical insulation, and DOWSIL FC-2024 coating for protecting battery housings and enclosures during thermal events. The introduction of VOLTRICELL supports growth by addressing manufacturers’ demand for materials that improve battery performance, safety and production scalability across the battery value chain. It builds on its deep materials science expertise and application development capabilities to foster innovation. For the second half of 2026, management plans to focus on growth and innovation in attractive end markets, investments to strengthen the portfolio and balanced capital allocation. Dow expects the growth and productivity benefits from Transform to Outperform to accelerate through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027. Dow expects approximately $200 million in additional benefits from Transform to Outperform during 2026. This raises the company’s expected total in-year benefits from self-help initiatives to more than $1.3 billion. Another industry leader, DuPont, raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 operating EBITDA and adjusted earnings guidance. The company now expects net sales in the range of $7.16-$7.19 billion, operating EBITDA between $1.75 billion and $1.77 billion and adjusted earnings of $7.17-$7.32 per share. The outlook reflects continued strength across healthcare, industrial water and aerospace end markets. Management expects mid-single-digit organic sales growth in the second half and remains focused on productivity, profitable growth and shareholder value creation. Eastman, on its second-quarter call, said that it expects earnings to improve significantly from 2025. The company remains on track to deliver cost reductions of $125 million to $150 million, net of inflation. For the third quarter, adjusted earnings are projected to approach the second-quarter level of $1.97 per share. Advanced Materials EBIT is expected to increase on improved price-cost and asset utilization, while Fibers earnings should benefit from higher acetate tow purchases. Additives & Functional Products earnings are expected to decline modestly due to seasonal agriculture weakness, while Chemical Intermediates earnings are projected to ease as supply-chain disruptions lessen. Air Products, for fiscal 2026, raised its adjusted earnings guidance to $13.39-$13.49 per share from the prior range of $13-$13.25. For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Air Products expects adjusted earnings of $3.55-$3.65 per share. The company now anticipates fiscal 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $3.5 billion, below its earlier projection of about $4 billion. Management expects new asset contributions, pricing actions and productivity initiatives to support performance, while remaining cautious because of macroeconomic uncertainty. artigo.texto: Siga Startups no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Siga Startups no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. A falta de infraestrutura para energia elétrica está colocando obstáculos à expansão da inteligência artificial até mesmo em projetos que contam com grandes empresas de tecnologia. A Microsoft desistiu de um contrato para ser a principal cliente de um data center da Nscale em Loughton, no Reino Unido, depois que atrasos na conexão à rede elétrica empurraram a previsão de fornecimento de energia para 2030. O problema está na capacidade da infraestrutura elétrica de acompanhar o ritmo de expansão dos data centers. No Reino Unido, os pedidos de conexão à rede de transmissão para consumo de energia cresceram 460% nos seis meses até junho de 2025, segundo o governo britânico. Como resultado, alguns empreendimentos enfrentam esperas de até 15 anos para conseguir uma conexão à rede elétrica. O empreendimento estava previsto para entrar em operação no início de 2027. O plano era instalar 23.040 unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) GB300, da Nvidia, com capacidade computacional de 50 megawatts para apoiar os serviços de nuvem Azure da Microsoft no país. A decisão, porém, não significa o fim da parceria entre as duas empresas. Em comunicado à Reuters, a Microsoft afirmou que continua comprometida com a Nscale e com o desenvolvimento de infraestrutura digital. Segundo a companhia, a saída diz respeito exclusivamente ao local de Loughton. A Nscale também declarou que mantém uma relação de longo prazo com a Microsoft e que o problema não afeta seus outros contratos. A empresa afirmou que segue comprometida com o projeto e com o mercado britânico, enquanto avalia fontes alternativas de energia para viabilizar a operação. Infraestrutura computacional Fundada em Londres para fornecer infraestrutura voltada à inteligência artificial, a Nscale oferece capacidade computacional, data centers, energia e software para treinar e executar modelos de IA. A empresa, inclusive, entrou com um pedido de IPO nos Estados Unidos em setembro de 2026, com planos de listagem na New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) sob o ticker NSCL. A Nscale disputa esse mercado com empresas como CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe e Lambda Labs, que também fornecem infraestrutura computacional para aplicações de inteligência artificial. O episódio reforça que a expansão da IA depende não apenas da disponibilidade de chips e investimentos, mas também de condições físicas para operar os sistemas. Sem energia e conexões à rede elétrica no prazo necessário, projetos de grande porte podem sofrer atrasos ou perder contratos antes mesmo de entrar em funcionamento. Apesar do revés em Loughton, a Nscale segue atraindo investidores. Em 25 de setembro, a empresa anunciou a captação de US$ 3,36 bilhões por meio de notas conversíveis, que são empréstimos que podem virar ações da companhia no futuro. A rodada foi liderada pela Third Point e contou com a participação da Nvidia, que ainda se comprometeu a aportar mais US$ 1 bilhão em novembro. Segundo a Nscale, o dinheiro será usado para ampliar sua plataforma, que inclui desde usinas de energia próprias, instaladas junto ao local de consumo, até data centers e grandes clusters de GPUs. A Nscale também já deu o primeiro passo para abrir capital. A empresa protocolou recentemente seu pedido de IPO, com listagem prevista na Bolsa de Nova York (NYSE). O número de ações e a faixa de preço ainda não foram definidos. Siga Startups no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. artigo.texto: Data center fervor is sweeping Central Florida, as voters pressure political leaders to keep the massive hubs of network infrastructure out of their cities and counties for fear they’ll gobble up local water resources and lead to higher electricity prices. And whether it’s in Florida’s governor race or local contests, candidates are being pinned down in forums and interviews for their positions on so-called hyper-scale data centers that polling shows voters loathe. A July University of North Florida poll found 68% of Florida voters disapprove of data centers being built in their area, including 84% of Democrats surveyed and 52% of Republicans. But perhaps most important in numerous races thought to be closely contested, 76% of voters with no party affiliation also don’t support them. Few people surveyed like data centers, the sprawling facilities that power artificial intelligence, among other things, said Sean Freeder, the director of the UNF Public Opinion Research Lab. “It’s the only question in the last several years in our polling where majorities dislike it across the board,” he said. “Democrats and independents are similar: They utterly hate them.” There are no hyper-scale centers in Central Florida, though a developer is marketing land in a rural section of Osceola County as a good site for one of the 5,000+ server facilities that are the focus of public ire. That’s prompted a petition urging county officials to turn down any such request should a data center developer try to buy the land. At least two other counties are considering moratoriums on data centers, even without any proposals in the pipeline. Data centers also have become one of the defining issues in the race to be Florida’s governor between Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly, who have staked out significantly different positions on the issue. Donalds has offered some conditional support while Jolly, labeling his opponent “Data Center Donalds,” says he doesn’t want them in Florida. Complaints about the facilities range from how much water and electricity they consume to the constant noise of loud cooling fans measuring 100 decibels or more. Donalds has said he supports existing state law that allows cities and counties to determine for themselves whether or not to build data centers in their jurisdictions and says that utility rates cannot increase because of a hyperscale data center. He also has said he wants Florida to regulate how close such a facility can be to homes. After New York passed a one-year moratorium on large-scale centers, Donalds said that’s not the right approach for Florida. “But you also have to understand that when you start doing stuff like what New York just did, that’s a signal to the business community that this is not a place to invest capital,” he said. “This is not a place to invest in businesses, and so we have to be balanced and be mindful about that.” But the tech industry and data center developers have also been a major support of Donalds — with $6 million in direct donations and advertising support from donors such as utilities like Next Era and Duke Energy, as well as firms like Google and Meta, according to the state government watchdog website Seeking Rents. Jolly and Florida Democrats have tried to use the issue as they work to win the governor’s mansion for the first time in 30 years. After dubbing the Republican with the data center nickname, they use it frequently in online campaign ads. Jolly has said he would implement a one year moratorium on new data centers if elected. In an interview last month with the Orlando Sentinel, Jolly made his strategy clear: “Every time I open my mouth it’s ‘Housing, health care, education and no data centers,’” he said. “That’s it.” Florida Democrats this week hosted what they called the Data Center Donalds tour, stopping in downtown Orlando for a news conference. “Ultimately, data centers are not here to create new jobs; they’re here to exploit our resources, to impact our quality of life in a negative way and do it so that a handful of oligarchs can continue to be rich and wealthy while the rest of us struggle,” Rep. Anna Eskamani, D-Orlando, said. This comes as local governments across the state, including those dominated by Republicans, grapple with how to handle data center proposals. For instance, in conservative Lake County, last month the Board of County Commissioners enacted a 90-day pause on any new data centers. But the board this week asked its staff to draw up an ordinance that would allow them under a conditional use permit, which would mean any proposed center would require a vote by the commission. In Democrat-controlled Orange County, commissioners signaled last month they were likely to impose a moratorium on any new hyperscale data centers, though they haven’t yet voted to do so. Both candidates on the ballot next month for mayor, Tiffany Moore Russell, a Democrat, and Chris Messina, a Republican, have said they support a moratorium. Last month, several dozen speakers addressed commissioners urging them to support such restrictions. Toward the end of public comment, one resident, Angie Hatfield, made it plain. “As elected officials, if you don’t vote yes on a data moratorium, who are you representing?” she said. In Osceola, the commercial real estate firm CBRE is marketing 2,232 acres off Canoe Creek Road in Kenansville as “Florida’s premier hyperscale data center development site.” The listing notes it includes 1,066 buildable acres, with electrical service by Duke Energy and “significant water resources permitted.” The listing has drawn opposition in the form of a petition with more than 600 signatures. It urges Osceola County’s Board of County Commissioners to reject the project, if it comes forward. “They should reject the data center, and no vote should happen without public hearings and full disclosure of its water use, energy demands and environmental impact,” it reads. artigo.texto: Data center stocks are being squeezed on Tuesday following a lackluster initial public offering overnight from a South Korean cloud company that has been compared to U.S. neocloud CoreWeave. Shares of Elice dropped 30% during their market debut overnight, as investors grow increasingly wary of artificial intelligence-dedicated computing power providers amid concerns about overcapacity. The bearish sentiment spilled into U.S. tech equities before some names clambered back into the green. CoreWeave shares are up 1.6% after dropping 4% just after market open Tuesday; Nebius shed about 1% while Iren was down about 4% in late morning trading. HSBC said in a Monday note that the troubles for the heavily levered CoreWeave are not going away. "Debt market woes and moderating LLM revenues are exacerbating structural concerns for neoclouds," HSBC analyst Abhishek Shukla wrote. Shukla has a reduce rating on CoreWeave with a price target of $39, implying 36.5% downside. Elice's IPO was small, having raised just $150 million, according to Reuters. Its market cap also equates to roughly $1.3 billion. The company provides a range of AI-related services, including cloud computing equipment, training libraries and application interfaces for businesses. Despite its size, investors are likely looking at it as a a signal of investor sentiment toward the AI build-out. Trouble for neoclouds, which some investors see as the weakest link in the emerging AI value chain, started earlier this month with less-than-stellar revenues reported by the private AI algorithm companies and pressure from higher interest rates. Frontier model Anthropic showed a deceleration in quarterly revenues, with sales dropping from 140% growth in the second quarter to 45% in the third. OpenAI also disappointed, reporting revenue that was $20 billion shy of what analysts expected, analyst Stephanie Roth at Wolfe said in a Sunday note. Profitability concerns for AI algorithm companies were the focus of a report last week from advisory firm Gartner predicting that 80% of neoclouds could cease independent operations by 2030. "Our research indicates that enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures" between 2027 and 2030, Will Sommer, senior director analyst at Gartner, said. Gartner stood by its analysis in a Monday interview with CNBC. "At the moment, we have more compute capacity than we have demand, and we have a lot of the tokens and processing power being given away in freemium solutions," Gartner chief forecaster John Lovelock told CNBC. "Everyone in the AI race is running for a last-man standing position. Pretty much every market that Gartner is tracking in our AI race is likely to collapse down to a duopoly."

artigo.texto: UPDATE: Hermantown Planning Commission recommends council approve data center permit 11:45 PM UPDATE - The Planning and Zoning Commission voted 6 to 1 recommending Hermantown City Council to approve the Special Use Permit. HERMANTOWN, Minn. (Northern News Now) - Hermantown’s Planning and Zoning Commission took up the Special Use Permit needed to begin data center construction on Tuesday night. The meeting included multiple hours of presentations and public comment. As of 11:00 pm Tuesday, they have not made their recommendation on the SUP. Hermantown city documents define a Special Use Permit as a permit that clears buildings for uses that they consider desirable, but that may pose potential hazards that would need to be mitigated. The planning and zoning commission held a public hearing on the Special Use Permit for Google’s proposed data center before making its recommendation to council. The meeting brought in both sides of the data center debate. Site Setup Before public comment, the commission went over nearly every aspect of the proposed data center building, from traffic impacts to the utilities setup and architecture of the site. The 8-building campus would include three 375 thousand square foot data center buildings, each of which would have a 150 thousand square foot mechanical building and an equipment yard beside it. “The buildings are designed to house the IT infrastructure required to store, process, and transmit the data utilized in everyday digital services for users worldwide,” said Hermantown Community Development Director Eric Johnson. Stormwater System A big topic of discussion among the commission was stormwater management. The City’s engineer said that out of the 234-acre site, 191 acres will be disturbed. He said that once water is collected and treated by the on-site stormwater system, that runoff will go into the Midway River. But the setup raised questions from commissioners. “We get snow runoff extraordinaire with the ground still solidly frozen,” said Planning and Zoning Commissioner Beth Wentzlaff. “These things, according to what I’m seeing, are not going to work very well.” Hermantown City Engineer David Bolf responded to her concern. “I have designed basins for 30 years, and I have never experienced a problem with frost,” he said. City leaders say the meeting will go late into the night if it needs to. After the presentation, the commission will hear from the public, where over 20 residents are signed up to speak. After the commission makes its recommendation, that’ll be taken to the City Council, which will be voting on the Special Use Permit on Monday. If that vote goes through, the city says Google will be cleared to use that land to build its 1.6 million-square-foot data center. Pending Litigation There are currently two lawsuits against the city from Stop the Hermantown Data Center. RELATED: Stop the Hermantown Data Center announces new lawsuit against city City leaders say despite the pending litigation, their legal counsel says they are cleared to proceed with the Special Use Permit and final plat decisions. Google representatives said if the SUP goes through, they will need to get other permits from other government agencies. “Our development timeline is subject to ongoing permitting and regulatory approvals that will trail the City’s SUP process,” said a Google Spokesperson. “Our earliest construction start is during the 2027 construction season; this is subject to the ongoing permitting processes, business demand, market conditions, and other associated factors.” Click here to download the Northern News Now app or our Northern News Now First Alert weather app. Copyright 2026 Northern News Now. artigo.texto: Maharashtra State Power Generation Co. Ltd., Mumbai, India (MAHAGENCO) has issued a 500 MW/1,600 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) tender with two-hour and four-hour storage across Maharashtra. It envisions developing the project under a Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model, including Operation & Maintenance (O&M) for 15 years. It has sought online bids until November 5, 2026. It plans to develop six battery energy storage systems (BESS) totaling 500 MW/1,600 MWh. It includes developing 100 MW/400 MWh units each in Uran (Raigad district), Koradi, Nashik, and Khaperkheda. The tender also includes developing a 50 MW/100 MWh BESS project each at Chandrapur (Lakhmapur) and Parli, connected to MSETCL STU substations (33 kV and above). Each bidder must submit the bid processing fee of Rs. 10 lakh plus 18% GST for the total project capacity quoted via NEFT/RTGS to MAHAGENCO's account. The EMD (Earnest Money Deposit) or bid security for the project is Rs. 5 lakh/MW. Previous BESS Projects in Maharashtra Previously, companies such as Oriana Power Limited and GK Energy Limited won a combined Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity of 1,050 MW / 2,100 MWh from MSEDCL. They secured this capacity under MSEDCL’s 2,000 MW / 4,000 MWh BESS tender, which was awarded within a month of its issuance. Oriana Power received two Letters of Award (LoAs) from MSEDCL to establish 900 MW / 1,800 MWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in Maharashtra. Under these two LoAs, Oriana Power’s capacity is divided into 500 MW / 1,000 MWh and 400 MW / 800 MWh, respectively. GK Energy Limited also secured a BESS project after receiving a Letter of Award (LoA) from MSEDCL to set up a 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS project with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support. Under this tender, the company was awarded the project at a tariff of Rs. 2,38,000/MW/month, resulting in an annual revenue of Rs. 42.84 crore (excluding GST) for 15 years from the commercial operation date (COD).

artigo.texto: Baker McKenzie Cairo advised Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (“CATL”), one of the world’s largest and most innovative battery technology companies, on its cooperation with Battery Manufacturing Egypt (BME) (being a joint venture between Manufacturing Commercial Vehicles (MCV) and Auto D) for the establishment of a battery systems manufacturing plant in Egypt. The project marks an important step in advancing Egypt’s industrial and clean technology capabilities and strengthening the country’s position within the evolving electric mobility and energy infrastructure value chain. Ghada El Ehwany, Managing Partner of Baker McKenzie Cairo, commented: “We are delighted to have supported CATL on this strategic project, which brings advanced battery technology and manufacturing capabilities to Egypt. The transaction reflects growing investment in the country’s industrial and clean technology sectors and demonstrates Egypt’s increasing role as a regional hub for advanced manufacturing and innovation.” Additionally, Zeinab Shohdy, M&A Counsel, commented: “This transaction called for a carefully tailored approach that balanced the parties’ commercial objectives while rigorously protecting CATL’s proprietary technology assets. We are proud to have helped establish a robust framework that enables CATL’s cutting-edge expertise and innovation to be deployed in Egypt while fully supporting its strategic business objectives.” Baker McKenzie acted as local counsel to CATL and advised on the structuring and implementation of the comprehensive contractual framework governing the parties’ technology cooperation, encompassing the commercialization of CATL’s advanced technology in Egypt while safeguarding its intellectual property rights and proprietary know-how. The scope of work included advising on the structuring and negotiation of the project agreements, navigating regulatory considerations across the transaction, and developing bespoke contractual protections designed to safeguard CATL’s long-term commercial interests. The Baker McKenzie Cairo team was led by the office’s Managing Partner Ghada El Ehwany, M&A Partner Hani Nassef, and Counsel Zeinab Shohdy, and further included Mohamed Elfar, Heba Samy, Omar Zaki and Mohamed El Baroudy. artigo.texto: O paranaense e administrador de empresas Lúcio Lopez, fundador e CEO da Greenline, empresa brasileira de tecnologia para o mercado de carbono, projeta faturamento de R$ 250 milhões e quer ampliar a escala de sua operação, que monitora 1,5 milhão de hectares de florestas em propriedades privadas no Brasil. Segundo estimativas divulgadas por ele, os projetos acompanhados registram sequestro médio anual de cerca de 25 milhões de toneladas de CO₂. Depois de investir mais de R$ 35 milhões de recursos próprios no desenvolvimento de sua tecnologia, a empresa prepara uma nova frente de negócios: créditos de carbono protegidos por seguro contra riscos fundiários, cibernéticos e políticos. Em setembro, anunciou uma parceria com a RCGI-USP Carbon Registry para fornecer evidências digitais que poderão ser consideradas no registro de projetos. A aposta combina escala, monitoramento por satélite e mecanismos de rastreabilidade para tornar o mercado mais confiável e, na visão de Lopez, mais acessível. “Até hoje, em oito anos, todo o investimento foi feito por mim e pela minha própria família. Se somar tudo, já são mais de 35 milhões de reais”, afirma o empresário. A trajetória que levou à criação da Greenline começou em 2018, quando Lopez acompanhava dos Estados Unidos notícias sobre desmatamento e incêndios florestais no Brasil. Com passagens pela indústria moveleira, pelo comércio exterior e pelo mercado financeiro, passou a estudar como incentivos econômicos poderiam tornar a preservação florestal uma alternativa mais rentável para os proprietários de terras. De acordo com dados da Embrapa Territorial, 66,3% do território brasileiro (cerca de 564 milhões de hectares) é coberto por vegetação nativa, sendo que 25,6% (218,2 milhões de hectares) estão preservados dentro de propriedades rurais privadas pelos próprios produtores. Esta é uma grande oportunidade para a Greenline poder conectar, o produtor que preserva e sequestra carbono com empresas que querem mitigar sua pegada de carbono, como as aéreas Gol, Latam, e Azul; bancos, como Banco do Brasil e Bradesco; indústrias como CSN, Gerdau e Vale; e a até petroquímicas como Petrobras e Braskem. Lopez se reuniu com todas. “Em cada setor, fomos buscar opiniões sobre se seria interessante ter um novo standard de crédito de carbono utilizando dados espaciais”, diz Lopez. Em termos de potencial, o agronegócio brasileiro poderá gerar até 314,3 milhões de créditos de carbono entre 2025 e 2035, com potencial de movimentar até R$ 3,5 bilhões no mercado internacional. A estimativa faz parte do estudo O Agronegócio Brasileiro no Mercado Internacional de Carbono – Oportunidades Econômicas, Elegibilidade e Impactos na NDC, divulgado pela Associação Brasileira do Agronegócio (ABAG). Uma nova camada de evidências para os créditos A Greenline desenvolveu uma plataforma de monitoramento, relato e verificação digital, conhecida como dMRV, que combina dados de satélites, sensoriamento remoto, inteligência artificial e informações geoespaciais. A tecnologia utiliza dados de agências como a Agência Espacial Americana (NASA) e a Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA), além de um índice próprio, o GLVCI (Greenline Vegetation Carbon Index), que, segundo Lopez, analisa 16 domínios e aplica mais de 100 índices de vegetação. A proposta é acompanhar as mudanças nas áreas monitoradas com atualizações frequentes e recuperar informações históricas para estimar alterações na vegetação e no estoque de carbono. Na prática, a tecnologia pode reduzir a dependência de levantamentos exclusivamente presenciais e gerar registros digitais que ajudam a documentar a situação de cada área ao longo do tempo. É essa capacidade de produzir evidências sistemáticas que levou à aproximação com a RCGI-USP Carbon Registry, registradora vinculada ao Centro de Pesquisa e Inovação em Gases de Efeito Estufa da Universidade de São Paulo. A colaboração, firmada em setembro deste ano, prevê que informações produzidas pela plataforma da Greenline possam ser consideradas na avaliação de projetos, desde que atendam às metodologias e aos critérios estabelecidos pela registradora. “O mercado de carbono depende da confiança nas informações apresentadas pelos projetos. Essa parceria fortalece justamente esse aspecto. A tecnologia da Greenline acrescenta uma camada adicional de evidências, oferecendo mais segurança de que os dados apresentados refletem efetivamente a realidade observada em campo”, afirma Ruy Rêde, gerente de Transferência de Tecnologia e Inovação do RCGI-USP. O executivo ressalta, porém, que a tecnologia não substitui o papel institucional da registradora. “Nosso papel continua sendo avaliar as evidências produzidas ao longo do processo, mas contar com uma tecnologia reconhecida de verificação digital aumenta a robustez e a credibilidade das informações que chegam à registradora.” A separação de responsabilidades é central para a credibilidade do sistema: a Greenline fornece dados técnicos, enquanto a registradora avalia as evidências segundo suas próprias regras. A parceria não representa aprovação automática dos projetos nem elimina a necessidade de auditorias e verificações independentes. Metodologias adaptadas aos biomas brasileiros Para Odair Carrel, diretor executivo da RCGI-USP Carbon Registry, a inovação não está apenas no uso de satélites, mas na combinação entre tecnologia e metodologias capazes de refletir melhor as características dos ecossistemas brasileiros e de outros países do Hemisfério Sul. “O que estamos fazendo é uma inovação no mercado de carbono mundial. Nós estamos trazendo as metodologias embasadas no IPCC e na UNFCCC, que são as bases metodológicas de captura e mensuração de carbono, para a realidade do mercado brasileiro e do Hemisfério Sul”, afirma Carrel. O executivo argumenta que muitas metodologias tradicionais foram concebidas considerando as condições do Hemisfério Norte. artigo.texto: 💻 A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do assistente de inteligência artificial Claude, está perto de ampliar ainda mais sua estrutura de computação. A Nscale, empresa de nuvem voltada à IA e apoiada pela Nvidia (NVDA), negocia a venda de capacidade computacional para a Anthropic em um acordo que pode chegar a cerca de US$ 45 bilhões, de acordo com pessoas a par das conversas. Acompanhe todas as notícias pelo celular! Baixe o app Se confirmado, este será o segundo grande contrato entre as duas empresas. Segundo documentos regulatórios ligados à oferta pública inicial planejada pela Nscale, a Anthropic já possui acordos de infraestrutura com a companhia que somam até aproximadamente US$ 44,6 bilhões. O negócio pode ser concluído nos próximos dias, segundo as fontes, que falaram sob condição de anonimato por se tratar de negociações privadas. As conversas seguem em andamento, os termos ainda podem mudar e nenhuma decisão definitiva foi tomada. Anthropic e Nscale não comentaram o assunto. Novo prédio terá 460 megawatts e chips Vera Rubin O novo contrato envolve uma instalação no complexo de data centers Monarch, que a Nscale desenvolve na Virgínia Ocidental, nos Estados Unidos. O segundo edifício do campus terá capacidade para entregar 460 megawatts de poder computacional e utilizará os chips de IA Vera Rubin, da Nvidia, a geração mais avançada da fabricante, segundo parte das fontes. Pelo desenho em discussão, a Anthropic também teria direito de preferência sobre um terceiro prédio previsto para o mesmo complexo. A dimensão do projeto ajuda a entender o interesse da empresa. De acordo com os documentos do IPO da Nscale, o campus Monarch poderá ultrapassar 8 gigawatts de capacidade elétrica bruta quando estiver totalmente concluído. Espaço foi aberto depois da desistência da Microsoft A entrada da Anthropic no complexo tem um antecedente curioso. Parte do campus Monarch seria inicialmente alugada pela Microsoft (MSFT), que em março havia anunciado a assinatura de uma carta de intenções para o projeto. No meio do ano, porém, a gigante de tecnologia desistiu da instalação, o que abriu espaço para que a Anthropic assumisse a operação. A Anthropic, uma das maiores clientes da Nscale, se transformou em um dos principais impulsionadores da demanda mundial por data centers dedicados à inteligência artificial. A empresa vem fechando uma série de acordos de grande porte para garantir capacidade computacional. Entre eles estão um contrato de US$ 50 bilhões com a Fluidstack, outro de US$ 10 bilhões com a startup de infraestrutura Volta e um acordo de US$ 45 bilhões com a SpaceX (SPCX), de Elon Musk. A busca por mais poder computacional acompanha o crescimento acelerado da companhia. Em julho, a Anthropic ultrapassou US$ 65 bilhões em receita anualizada, e em maio a empresa foi avaliada em US$ 965 bilhões. A desenvolvedora do Claude também é candidata a realizar sua própria abertura de capital nos próximos meses, em uma operação que pode estar entre as maiores da história recente do setor de tecnologia. Acordo pode reforçar o IPO da Nscale, avaliado em US$ 30 bi Do lado da Nscale, um novo contrato bilionário chega em um momento estratégico. A empresa busca uma avaliação de aproximadamente US$ 30 bilhões em seu IPO nos Estados Unidos, mas um grupo de investidores vem pressionando para que a companhia reduza essa meta de valuation. Um acordo dessa magnitude com um cliente como a Anthropic tende a fortalecer os argumentos da empresa diante do mercado. A Nscale protocolou o pedido público de listagem em setembro, mas ainda não iniciou formalmente a divulgação da oferta, embora o prazo regulatório de espera já tenha terminado. A empresa responde a questionamentos da SEC, órgão regulador do mercado de capitais americano, e pretende começar o roadshow com investidores assim que essas questões forem resolvidas. No mês passado, a companhia levantou US$ 3,36 bilhões em uma rodada pré-IPO liderada pela Third Point, de Dan Loeb, com participação de investidores como Nvidia, Apollo Global Management, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital e Abu Dhabi Investment Council. 💰 O avanço dos investimentos em infraestrutura de IA, porém, vem acompanhado de cautela no mercado. Investidores têm demonstrado preocupação crescente com o volume de dívidas usado para financiar a expansão acelerada dos data centers, tema que tem pesado sobre ações de fabricantes de chips e sobre os títulos de dívida de empresas de computação em nuvem.

artigo.texto: With the Nov. 3 general election coming up, NHPR is sitting down with the candidates for governor to discuss top issues in the race and ask questions submitted by listeners and readers. Cinde Warmington, an attorney and former executive councilor from Concord, is the Democratic nominee. Here are some takeaways from her interview with NHPR. A full transcript of this conversation with All Things Considered host Julia Barnett follows below. On housing - Warmington said she would create a new state position of “housing czar” to focus on housing inventory and affordability. - She also promised investments in the Affordable Housing Fund, a state-administered loan program managed by New Hampshire Housing, to leverage federal funds. On data centers - Warmington is calling for an immediate moratorium on AI data centers in New Hampshire. She said the state needs to protect itself from skyrocketing electric rates and begin environmental impact studies as needed. On local or state agreements with ICE - “At the state level I do not believe that we should be cooperating with an organization that has been shown to be lawless, to be putting masked thugs on the street, terrorizing communities around our state.” On her past work as an opioid company lobbyist - Warmington said her representation of Purdue Pharma was 25 years ago. She said the pharmaceutical company lied to doctors and the FDA. - “I've been very, very clear that if I had known at the time what we all learned later, I would have had nothing, nothing to do with this work. And I certainly regret having anything to do with this work, knowing what we all know now.” What questions do you have about this year's elections? Let us know at voices@nhpr.org, and we could help you get the answers. Find all of our 2026 election coverage here. This transcript has been lightly edited for clarity. Rising housing costs continue to be a major issue for Granite Staters. As governor, what new ideas would you bring to address the housing crisis here? Well, as you said, housing costs are through the roof here. We've hit record highs under Kelly Ayotte's administration. I'm hearing about it everywhere I go across the state. Young people who can't afford to buy a home. Young people who can barely afford to pay rent. I'm hearing from seniors who are having trouble staying in their homes because of the skyrocketing property taxes, yet there's no place for them to downsize to. There's just no place for them to go. Small businesses, large businesses can't hire people because of the housing crisis in our state. This really needs to be taken head on. You may know that in our state, we actually have nobody accountable for knowing how many housing units we have, how many we need, and how we're going to get there. So first thing is, we're going to put in a housing czar who is going to be accountable for making sure we have a plan going forward. We're going to invest in the Affordable Housing Fund, because that's a fund where for every dollar we invest, we can leverage three federal dollars for that. We have been leaving millions of dollars on the table that should be invested in the Affordable Housing Fund, and we're going to fund that Housing Champions program, which was working so well. Almost half of our housing starts came from Housing Champions communities last year, and Kelly Ayotte defunded that program. There's so many more. We need to have all stakeholders at the table, but this is an all hands on deck problem that we need to tackle head on. And the state has struggled with a tight budget historically. Where would this money come from to support these efforts? This money was in the budget. And Kelly Ayotte decided to defund, for instance, the Housing Champions program. This is a matter of priorities and where you're going to put the priorities. Housing is a number one issue in the state, and it is going to affect not only the ability of people to stay here and raise their families here, but it affects the viability of our economy going forward. We absolutely have to be invested in this. As winter approaches, many folks are facing soaring fuel and electricity costs on top of other affordability concerns they may already have. What will you do as governor to help mitigate energy costs for Granite Staters, both in the short and long term? Well, I mean, first thing, we have to stand up and speak out about why energy costs are through the roof right now. As you mentioned, gas prices, heating oil prices are through the roof. That is largely because of Donald Trump's reckless war and his tariffs, both of things that Kelly Ayotte has simply refused to stand up and speak out about and defend Granite Staters. Also skyrocketing electric prices, up 15% since Kelly Ayotte came into office, due largely because of her failed energy policies that just are simply hostile towards energy efficiency and renewable energy. That's where we need to be putting the emphasis so that we have an energy policy for the future that will make sure we are bringing down electric rates and not also appointing people to our public utilities commission, who will continue to cater to the utilities. We need people on that commission that are looking out for our ratepayers. And when it comes to renewables, you've proposed getting to net-zero emissions by 2040. That's 14 years away. How realistic is that? Well, I proposed 2040 in the last election, and that is when we had sort of record investments by the federal government in helping communities to do that. Under the Trump administration, of course, that money has gone away. So they've made the 2040 date impossible. But there needs to be a date out there somewhere where we are decreasing our dependence on fossil fuels. I do want to clear up a misunderstanding or a misrepresentation of my position. I am not against all emissions. I'm not against gas-powered cars. I am not against gas stoves. I cook with a gas stove myself. And net zero does not mean zero.

artigo.texto: District 12 Senator Amy Sinclair Earlier this month, it was announced that a $15 billion deal was in the works to bring a steel mill to Iowa. Iowa Senator for District 12 Amy Sinclair says that many are looking at the deal positively, while some other have also questioned it, asking what the difference is between this deal, and that of data centers. She tells Raccoon Valley Radio what that difference is. “I will say there’s some conversation surrounding data centers and how those are going in. The use of tax dollars for those, the use of water. There are some real concerns and some issues that I think will arise in the coming session to have a real honest conversation about how much farmland they’re taking up, about how many jobs they’re actually producing, about whether or not tax incentives at all should go into those data centers, given the fact that they’re owned by multi-billion dollar organizations that would be building data centers regardless.” Sinclair mentions that additionally, while this steel mill deal would qualify for megasite incentives under Iowa law, data centers do not. She adds that many incentives that go towards data centers are actually from local governments instead of the state.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de conectores de sinal: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de conectores de sinal até 2035: demanda por largura de banda em data centers impulsiona o crescimento Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Conectores de Sinal, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compras mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de suprimentos regionalmente mais diversificada. O mercado global de conectores de sinal entra em uma fase de crescimento estrutural, à medida que a infraestrutura digital, a eletrificação veicular e a automação industrial intensificam a demanda por interconexões rápidas e confiáveis. Na base de referência de 2026, o mercado é reconhecido como viabilizador essencial da integridade de sinal em telecomunicações, data centers, eletrônica automotiva, sistemas industriais e dispositivos de consumo. Diferentemente dos conectores de potência, os conectores de sinal são definidos por largura de banda, miniaturização e densidade de contatos, e sua demanda acompanha os ciclos de inovação da eletrônica a jusante, e não simplesmente os volumes unitários. O horizonte de previsão 2026-2035 abrange um período em que os investimentos em data centers, a implantação de 5G/6G, os sistemas avançados de assistência ao motorista e a digitalização das fábricas vão remodelar o mix de produtos em direção a conectores de RF de alta frequência, fibra óptica e placas de passo fino. As cadeias de suprimentos continuam concentradas nos polos industriais da Ásia-Pacífico, mas a demanda se globaliza, com América do Norte e Europa investindo em capacidade regional para componentes críticos de conectividade. A intensidade competitiva é elevada, com multinacionais aproveitando portfólios amplos e empresas especializadas mirando aplicações de nicho de alto desempenho. Este relatório oferece uma visão baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, comércio, preços e dinâmica competitiva, fornecendo a fabricantes, distribuidores e investidores um arcabouço analítico transparente para decisões estratégicas até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado mundial de conectores de sinal pressupõe a expansão contínua da infraestrutura digital e do conteúdo eletrônico por dispositivo, sustentando uma taxa composta de crescimento anual (CAGR) moderada de um dígito até 2035. Espera-se que a demanda seja liderada pela modernização da largura de banda em data centers, onde taxas de sinalização mais altas exigem conectores avançados de RF, fibra óptica e placas de alta densidade, e pela eletrônica automotiva, à medida que as arquiteturas veiculares migram para controladores zonais e de domínio. A automação industrial e os dispositivos médicos acrescentam uma demanda resiliente, orientada por especificações. O cenário-base incorpora a normalização das cadeias de suprimentos, adições graduais de capacidade na Ásia-Pacífico e a regionalização contínua da produção de componentes críticos. Espera-se que os preços permaneçam competitivos nas categorias de conectores de uso geral, enquanto os conectores premium de alta frequência e para ambientes severos sustentam as margens. Entre os riscos estão pausas cíclicas nos investimentos de telecomunicações e data centers, a volatilidade das matérias-primas e atritos na política comercial, mas não se assume que esses fatores descarrilhem a trajetória de longo prazo. Projeta-se que o índice de mercado suba de 100 em 2025 para aproximadamente 168 em 2035, o que corresponde a uma CAGR de cerca de 5,3%. Essa perspectiva implica crescimento em volume nos segmentos maduros e crescimento em valor concentrado nas famílias de conectores de alta velocidade, miniaturizados e específicos para aplicações. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Expansão da largura de banda em data centers e investimentos em hiperescala impulsionando a demanda por conectores de RF de alta velocidade, fibra óptica e placas de passo fino - Migração da arquitetura eletrônica automotiva para ADAS, controladores zonais e eletrificação, elevando o conteúdo de conectores por veículo - Implantação de 5G e acesso fixo sem fio exigindo conectores de RF e modulares aprimorados na infraestrutura de telecomunicações - Automação industrial e adoção da Indústria 4.0 sustentando a demanda por conectores circulares e retangulares robustos - Miniaturização da eletrônica de consumo e dos dispositivos vestíveis impulsionando os volumes de conectores placa a placa de passo fino e modulares - Digitalização de dispositivos médicos e demanda de equipamentos de teste por conectores de sinal de alta confiabilidade Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Pausas cíclicas nos gastos de telecomunicações e data centers podem causar volatilidade de demanda no curto prazo - A volatilidade dos preços de cobre, ouro e plásticos de engenharia pressiona as margens - Atritos na política comercial e controles de exportação perturbam as cadeias transfronteiriças de conectores - A complexidade de projeto e os ciclos de qualificação prolongam o tempo de lançamento de conectores de alto desempenho Estrutura da Demanda por Indústria de Uso Final Telecomunicações e Data Centers (participação estimada: 28%) Telecomunicações e data centers representam o maior e mais dinâmico conjunto de demanda por conectores de sinal. A demanda atual está ancorada em equipamentos de rádio e transporte 5G, implantações de fibra até o ponto final e construções de data centers em hiperescala, onde taxas de sinalização mais altas exigem conectores de RF de baixa perda, conectores de fibra óptica de alta densidade e conectores de placa de passo fino. artigo.texto: EU ETS Revision 2026: Industrial Transformation Requires the Right Framework Conditions The European Commission has presented a draft for the further development of the EU ETS 1 beyond 2030, thereby providing an impetus for the future design of the European emissions trading system. The draft forms the basis for the upcoming discussions on a central instrument of European climate policy. With its proposal of 17 July 2026 to revise the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS1), the European Commission has proposed extensive changes to the existing system for the period after 2030. At the heart of the proposal are adjustments to the emissions reduction pathway (LRF), the introduction of conditionalities for free allocation, the integration of permanent CO₂ removals, the use of international carbon credits, and modifications to the Market Stability Reserve. In addition, free allocation for sectors covered by the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) would be phased out more slowly than currently envisaged. Furthermore, the Commission proposes a partial extension of the ETS to aviation and maritime transport, as well as the inclusion of waste incineration, thereby broadening the scope of the system in several areas. The BDI welcomes the Commission’s intention to maintain the ETS as the central market-based instrument for achieving climate objectives beyond 2030. At the same time, we see several shortcomings in the Commission’s proposal. The success of the ETS as a driver of industrial decarbonisation depends critically on whether the conditions needed for industrial transformation are actually in place. These include, in particular, a robust hydrogen and CO₂ infrastructure, renewable electricity at competitive prices, and functioning markets for climate neutral products. In many ETS covered sectors, these prerequisites are not available yet. Against this background, the BDI opposes additional conditionalities for free allocation proposed by the Commission. Free allocation serves the sole purpose of protecting against carbon leakage and compensating companies for CO₂-costs that international competitors outside Europe do not face. Conditionalities can therefore not function as an investment instrument and substitute for missing economic or infrastructural framework conditions. Additional requirements would weaken carbon leakage protection without addressing the underlying causes of insufficient transformation investments. One of BDI’s key priorities is safeguarding the international competitiveness of German industry. To date, no effective solution exists for exports from the EU to third country markets. European companies are required to bear the costs of the EU ETS1 while competing internationally with producers from countries that do not face a comparable carbon price. This creates significant competitive disadvantages. BDI therefore proposes a dedicated export solution to close this regulatory gap and preserve the international competitiveness of European manufacturers. As effective carbon leakage protection continues to require a sufficient volume of freely allocated allowances, we also advocate adjusting the balance between auctioning and free allocation. Specifically, we propose lowering the minimum share of allowances that must be auctioned, thereby increasing the volume available for free allocation accordingly, including to provide allowances for an export solution. Only in this way can both a realistic benchmark design and effective carbon leakage protection be ensured. We also see potential in the use of international emissions reduction credits to strengthen Europe’s competitiveness in third countries while providing for cost-effective decarbonisation options. Without introducing additional requirements for such credits, preference should be given to emissions reduction projects implemented with European technology. The coming months will be decisive for shaping the European emissions trading system after 2030. BDI is committed to ensuring that the ETS supports both climate protection and industrial competitiveness. The decarbonisation of industry can only succeed if climate policy ambitions and economic realities are brought into alignment.

artigo.texto: A China está a intensificar os investimentos no armazenamento de energia e na conservação dos ecossistemas, procurando conciliar a transição energética com a proteção ambiental. As duas prioridades foram destacadas em iniciativas divulgadas pela agência estatal Xinhua. Durante a Conferência Mundial de Armazenamento de Energia, realizada em Ningde, foram apresentados dados que atribuem à China 56% da expansão mundial da capacidade de armazenamento em baterias em 2025. No primeiro semestre de 2026, a produção chinesa de baterias destinadas a este setor ultrapassou 420 GWh, mais 110% do que no período homólogo. Paralelamente, o Presidente Xi Jinping defendeu o reforço da conservação ecológica durante uma visita à Mongólia Interior. Na reserva natural do lago Huangqihai, destacou a importância da recuperação das zonas húmidas, da proteção da biodiversidade e do cumprimento da legislação ambiental. A estratégia inclui ainda novas inspeções ambientais e a aplicação do Código Ecológico e Ambiental, em vigor desde agosto. Apesar dos progressos anunciados, persistem desafios relacionados com os custos das tecnologias, a fiscalização e a sustentabilidade dos resultados a longo prazo.

artigo.texto: Pro-Russian accounts targeting Ukrainians on Facebook and Telegram sharply declined after Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers, according to a new report from a Ukrainian government agency. It’s the most direct evidence so far behind a claim that went viral last week, but it falls well short of proving it. The report comes from Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD), which operates under the country’s National Security and Defense Council. It was published Oct. 15, and United24 Media covered it on Oct. 17. The CCD used software from the Ukrainian security firm Osavul to track accounts it flagged as showing "signs of inauthentic behavior." According to Osavul's website, the firm "builds AI-powered risk intelligence for hybrid threats." According to United24, the CCD analyzed 22,664 messages from 5,201 accounts posted between Oct. 6 and 12, across 26 topics in Ukraine’s information space. The report found two sharp drops in activity, each following a strike that fully shut down a Yandex facility. On Oct. 8, the day a fire took Yandex’s data center in Sasovo, in Russia’s Ryazan region, offline, messages fell 83.6 percent, from 4,032 to 660. The number of active accounts fell by a similar share. Activity rebounded past pre-strike levels by Oct. 10, but on Oct. 12, a day after a strike fully halted operations at a Yandex data center in Vladimir, messages fell by 42.6 percent and active accounts dropped by 41 percent. A smaller group of 98 accounts that posted pro-war propaganda, conspiracy theories, or calls for violence followed the same pattern. The CCD concluded that strikes on data centers can significantly disrupt Russian influence networks, but the effect appears to be short-lived. Mashable was unable to verify the CCD’s findings independently. Before publication, we emailed Osavul to request the underlying dataset, the criteria it uses to flag inauthentic behavior, and any information about where the accounts were hosted. Osavul did not respond by publication time. The report never defines "inauthentic behavior." While the term is quite broad, some general signals that researchers typically attribute to bot accounts include newly created profiles, unusually high posting volume, blank or AI-generated profile photos, and activity across many unrelated political narratives. Without Osavul’s criteria, it’s unclear whether these accounts are automated, run by coordinated humans, or a mix of both. Still, if the numbers hold up, they point to something real. The CCD argues that the drops show strikes on data centers can significantly constrain Russia’s information operations by disrupting the automated networks behind them. However, the agency also acknowledges how quickly the accounts came back, suggesting the disruptions were "substantial but short-lived." Why it matters The findings arrive after a week of overheated claims. Last week, Mashable looked at viral claims that Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers had knocked Russia’s bot army offline. The conclusion we and other outlets reached was that the data behind those claims couldn’t support them. That claim spread like wildfire on social media, amplified by European officials and even backed up by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, President Zelenskyy said "everyone noticed" a drop in Russian bot activity. Social media users echoed similar observations about the seemingly stark decline in pro-GOP and pro-AfD posts after the strikes. It was an easy idea to believe, given how platforms like Facebook and X incentivize and reward polarizing political ragebait, and Russia’s online influence operations are well-documented. The claim also seemed to have supporting data. United24 Media, the Ukrainian government-run outlet whose reporting drove much of the conversation, cited an analysis by The Deep Dive of Cloudflare Radar data. That data showed automated traffic from Yandex’s network had nearly vanished by Oct. 11. As Mashable reported at the time, that data couldn’t support the claim. "Automated traffic" means any request that software, rather than a person, sends to a website, and most of it is mundane. Yandex, often called "Russia's Google," runs the Federation's biggest search engine, so its network constantly sends out crawlers to index the web. Knocking its data centers offline would stop that traffic, whether or not a single troll account went quiet. We found no published evidence tying influence campaigns on social media to Yandex servers, and United24 acknowledged the same limitation. Cloudflare has since published its own analysis. It said its data doesn’t appear to support claims that the strikes crippled social media manipulation, though it couldn’t rule out a connection. Zelenskyy’s office has also narrowed his remarks. According to BBC Verify, his office said the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media" rather than a fall in bot activity.

artigo.texto: GCL Technology to acquire 81.91% of Sichuan GCL Lithium Battery Technology for CNY 2.5 billion GCL Technology Holdings has entered a non-binding memorandum of understanding to purchase approximately 81.91% of Sichuan GCL Lithium Battery Technology, an LFP cathode material manufacturer, from Golden Concord Group — the parent company controlled by GCL Technology chairman Zhu Gongshan and his family. According to a filing by the Hong Kong-listed company, the preliminary price stands at roughly CNY 2.5 billion. Cash would account for about CNY 650 million, while approximately CNY 1.85 billion would come through newly issued GCL Technology shares priced at no less than HK$1.30 apiece, or as many as about 1,671 million shares. An independent valuation will determine the final price. As the seller is controlled by the chairman's family trust, the transaction would constitute a connected transaction under Hong Kong listing rules. GCL Technology said it anticipates seeking a specific mandate from independent shareholders for the new share issuance. Due diligence is allotted 30 days, with three months of exclusivity for negotiating a formal agreement. The seller has guaranteed the target's combined adjusted net profit will reach at least CNY 620 million across 2027 and 2028. It has further pledged to develop a sixth-generation LFP cathode material achieving a compacted density above 2.8 g/cm3 by the close of 2028, with compensation payable should either commitment fall short. LFP capacity Meishan-based Sichuan GCL Lithium, located in Sichuan province, operates 120,000 tons of annual LFP production capacity at its first-phase facility, which sits on about 355 mu within a planned 1,000-mu site. A June report from GCL noted that production started in July 2023 and that the company supplies Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL) and Haichen Energy Storage. Through subsidiary Leshan Xinneng New Materials Technology, GCL Technology already produces LFP cathode material. Shipments from the first 200,000-ton phase commenced in June at an average tax-inclusive price of CNY 60,320 per ton, and the operation has been profitable since starting up, according to the company. GCL Technology said the acquisition would assist it in reducing reliance on pricing cycles for polysilicon and wafer products while improving earnings stability. The company recorded a net loss attributable to shareholders of CNY 2.08 billion in the first half of 2026, 17.2% larger than a year prior. It described the polysilicon industry as having fallen into involution once again during the first half of 2026, with prices plunging below the cash costs of most enterprises. Granular silicon averaged CNY 31.97/kg excluding tax, compared with a cash production cost of CNY 25.23/kg. In May, the company outlined plans to become a multi-product new energy materials platform centered on silicon, lithium and carbon. It referenced Chinese government data indicating the country's cumulative new-type energy storage capacity hit 153 GW/396 GWh by the end of June, an increase of about 61% year on year. The transaction follows an unsuccessful attempt to address polysilicon overcapacity via consolidation. Last year GCL Technology raised funds to back a government-supported plan under which China's six largest polysilicon makers would contribute about CNY 50 billion to acquire and idle roughly one-third of national capacity. China's antitrust regulator subsequently stopped that plan, and competitor Tongwei has since taken steps to acquire polysilicon producer Qinghai Lihao. - 1. artigo.texto: CATL launches “Dual-Electric Range Extender” to drive heavy-duty truck electrification On October 20, CATL officially unveiled its “Dual-Electric Range Extender” technology and the expanding plan for its “QiJi” heavy-duty truck battery-swapping ecosystem. The “Dual-Electric Range Extender” technology Over 430,000 electric heavy trucks already run on CATL batteries, representing over 70% of the market in the world. According to CATL, the debate between diesel and electric heavy trucks is effectively over, with the market entering an “electric-versus-electric” competitive phase. Data shows that the penetration rate of electric heavy trucks in China surged from 5.2% in 2022 to 50.28% in September 2026. The Dual-Electric Range Extender system utilises an “A+B” architecture: - A (bottom-mounted swappable battery): A swappable, high-capacity battery (432 kWh or 513 kWh) for primary driving, available via a flexible leasing model to reduce upfront costs. - B (range-extender battery): A fixed battery pack (77 kWh) that provides backup power. This system allows for deep discharge of the primary battery (down to 5% SOC) without the “range anxiety” associated with traditional electric trucks, as the system switches to the range-extender pack when needed. This approach, combined with a 5-minute battery swap capability, aims to match the operational efficiency of diesel trucks while lowering the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO). CATL estimates that compared to diesel trucks, the E-E system can save users over 460,000 yuan (68,700 USD) over a three-year cycle. Scaling the “QiJi” ecosystem To support this technology, CATL is expanding its “QiJi” battery-swapping network. The company has standardised battery blocks into two sizes: the 260# (432 kWh) for 3,800 mm wheelbase vehicles and the 300# (513 kWh) for 4,200 mm wheelbase vehicles. The infrastructure rollout: - Current status: 5 major trunk lines are operational, with over 5 million km of stable operation. - Near-term goal: 900 battery-swapping stations by the end of 2026. - Long-term goal: 2,000 stations by 2027, covering the national highway network, with an ultimate target of 10,000 stations. At the launch, CATL signed agreements with 14 major partners, including SF Express, ZTO Express, and YTO Express, with an initial order volume of 13,000 units.
